title: GH#33998: fix: shorten footprint reservation critical section
body:
## Summary

Parallel dispatch lost whole cycles to reservation_lock_busy because the per-repo footprint lock held a fork-heavy critical section (sed/tr per candidate x in-flight pair, 2-3 jq + grep per reservation record, repos.json jq read). Repo low-info basenames and live-issue extraction now run before the lock; _footprint_find_overlap is one awk pass with identical output contract and semantics (last-pipe split, ./ then .agents/ normalisation, case-insensitive low-info basename skip on candidates, last matching candidate names the blocker); each reservation record is read with one jq. event=reserved now logs waited_ms/hold_ms and event=lock_busy logs waited_ms so production logs can confirm the fix. Atomicity is unchanged: reservation read, overlap test, and write stay under one lock.



## Files Changed

## Runtime Testing

Base main failed case 35 on macOS only because BSD wc -l pads counts; assertions now compare with -eq. Diagnostic run logged: event=reserved issue=#810 ... waited_ms=7 hold_ms=7. shellcheck clean on both files.

title: GH#33993: fix: isolate detached headless workers in a systemd user scope
body:
## Summary

Manual-dispatch and CI-repair workers launched with headless-runtime-helper.sh run --detach stayed in the caller's cgroup (plain background subshell), so a KillMode=control-group pulse unit killed them on stop/TimeoutStartSec. _detach_worker now launches under systemd-run --user --scope when _dlw_systemd_user_service_available succeeds (shared probe, AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SYSTEMD_WORKER_SERVICE bypass retained), verifies /proc/<pid>/cgroup names the new scope, and logs worker_detached/worker_detach_unconfirmed. Fallback: setsid when available, plain background otherwise (macOS). Dispatched PID is now the worker process itself.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-tracking.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified on Ubuntu (systemd 259, OrbStack VM, user manager via linger): production _detach_worker run as the main process of a Type=oneshot KillMode=control-group parent unit, then the unit was stopped. Base main: worker cgroup .../app.slice/aidevops-verify-pulse-base.service, worker KILLED with parent unit (reproduces the issue). This branch: worker cgroup .../app.slice/aidevops-worker-verify-1776-1776-8860.scope, log worker_detached isolation=systemd_scope, Dispatched PID equals worker PID, exported env marker inherited, worker SURVIVED parent unit stop. macOS: test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh 90/90 (production detach + readiness envelope), test-systemd-unit-generation.sh pass, shellcheck -x clean.

## Regression Evidence

The regression needs a live systemd user manager (lingering user session with a D-Bus user bus), a parent `Type=oneshot` `KillMode=control-group` unit, and a unit stop while the detached worker runs; the observable is the worker's `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` and survival. The repository's existing suites run without a user manager (`_dlw_systemd_user_service_available` returns 1 there), and adding a privileged systemd-in-CI harness would be new test infrastructure. Evidence instead:

- Before/after on Ubuntu with systemd 259: base `main` kept the worker in `aidevops-verify-pulse-base.service` and it was killed by the unit stop; this branch moved it to `aidevops-worker-<session>-<pid>-<rand>.scope` and it survived.
- Existing `test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` (90/90) exercises the production `_detach_worker` launch, PID contract and readiness envelope on the non-systemd path.
- Production signal: the pulse log now shows `[lifecycle] worker_detached ... isolation=systemd_scope` for each manual or CI-repair detach on systemd hosts; `worker_detach_unconfirmed` flags any launch whose cgroup could not be confirmed.

## Decisions

Used a transient scope instead of a transient service: `systemd-run --user` services start with the user manager's environment and working directory, which would drop the exported worker env contract (attempt ID, git-auth sandbox, PR-repair variables) that `cmd_run` validated before detaching. A scope keeps both, and systemd-run execs the worker, so the scope's process is the real worker. An early worker exit never triggers a second launch; the caller's readiness check reports it with systemd-run errors in the worker log. `KillMode=control-group` on the pulse unit is unchanged.

Resolves #33993

title: GH#33997: fix: refuse checkpoint approval templates that dispatch-approved would reject
body:
## Summary

`approval-template` printed a `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line for any release ID. `dispatch-approved` accepts only a trusted `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` from the checkpoint runner closing the named attempt (`pr_checkpoint_events.py` `release_for`/`blocked_release_fields`). Approvals naming `worker_draft_checkpoint`, `crash_during_execution` or `worker_failed` releases could never dispatch. Because any trusted approval comment also disables the legacy continuation path (`pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh:141-148`), an invalid approval made recovery worse until someone deleted it.

The template now runs the same `release_for` check against the issue's comments before printing. When dispatch-approved would reject the release, it exits 1 and gives the reason on stderr. `_pcc_approval_template` passes the paginated issue comments to the validator.

## Scope correction (primary dead end moved to a follow-up)

While implementing, I found my approved review's item 1 rested on a false premise. The proactive sweep already refuses to reset an issue that has a closing-linked open PR (`pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:132-145,185-187`), so closing-linked drafts only see the bounded Layer 6 delay. The incident's permanent dead end comes from the pulse's own `checkpoint: recover dirty worker worktree for #N` drafts, which reference the issue as non-closing `For #N` by design (`shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:621-629`, GH#32933):

- `_stale_recovery_find_open_pr` uses `closingIssuesReferences`, so the sweep cannot see the draft and resets the issue without a release.
- `_pcc_dispatch` then rejects the draft as unlinked (`pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh:70`), even if a stall release existed.

Fixing that makes `For #N` worker-takeover checkpoints eligible for automatic continuation. That is the trust/eligibility policy change the review deferred, so it is filed as a separate worker-ready follow-up. This PR therefore uses `For #33997`.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py` — `template()` validates the release; shared `sorted_comments()`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — `_pcc_approval_template` supplies issue comments
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py` — template accept/refuse cases

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (approval-chain generator; it can only refuse more, never authorize more)
- **Verification:** `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py` 12/12. The new case checks that a generated line round-trips through `validate()`, and that `worker_draft_checkpoint`, `crash_during_execution`, `worker_failed`, wrong attempt and wrong release ID are refused. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` passes all 56 tests. `shellcheck -x` is clean.

For #33997

title: GH#34008: fix: continue For #N orphan-recovery checkpoint drafts instead of a permanent dispatch hold
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33997. The pulse's own orphan-recovery drafts (checkpoint: recover dirty worker worktree for #N, origin:worker-takeover, non-closing For #N body by design per GH#32933) were invisible to stale recovery and rejected by continuation, so a killed worker's issue was reset to status:available and then held forever by worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked. Changes: (1) pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh adds one shared linkage rule (_PR_CHECKPOINT_FOR_LINK_JQ_DEFS / _pr_checkpoint_recovery_draft_links_issue / _pr_checkpoint_pr_links_issue): a PR links issue N via a closing link, or when closingIssuesReferences is empty, the body has an exact For #N line (same regex the signed revision path uses), and it is an open same-repo draft labelled origin:worker-takeover with no origin:worker or protective label. _pr_checkpoint_pr_metadata_is_eligible uses it, so continuation dispatch and the verify-pr-checkpoint-target fence accept the draft; the expected_author check is kept. (2) dispatch-dedup-stale.sh sources the lib, requests body and isCrossRepository in the open-PR scan, and _stale_recovery_linked_pr_rows classifies such a draft as exact, so stale recovery emits STALE_PR_CONTINUATION (draft_checkpoint) and the proactive sweep skips the reset. (3) Already-reset issues: dispatch-stalled accepts, only for these recovery drafts, the killed attempt's own expired DISPATCH_CLAIM/non-terminal DISPATCH_LEASE as stall evidence when it is the newest trusted coordination event and is no newer than the draft head. Any newer claim, lease, release or interactive claim keeps the hold, so it fires at most once per head; the stall-release path and its stalls>=2 attention bound are unchanged. (4) Completion semantics: the continuation worker did not rewrite For #N. The target row now carries a link kind, and For-linked continuations get a prompt step to replace the exact For #N line with Resolves #N and confirm closingIssuesReferences before marking the PR ready.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — shellcheck -x on all 5 changed scripts: clean. test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh: All 75 tests passed (new cases: For #N worker-takeover draft accepted; origin:worker label, ready PR, cross-repo head, protected label, bare #N mention, #1234 prefix collision and closing link to another issue rejected; prompt rewrite step present only for For-linked targets; expired-claim evidence accepted/rejected for unexpired, newer-than-head, newer release/interactive claim/terminal lease and untrusted cases; end-to-end dispatch-stalled on an already-reset For draft dispatches exact-head continuation and claims the issue; ordinary worker draft still needs a stall release). test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh: all 8 new cases pass (For draft emits STALE_PR_CONTINUATION without issue mutation; sweep classifier returns 85|draft_checkpoint; 6 unsafe variants never continue); its 8 remaining failures are pre-existing and identical on origin/main (stub lacks the graphql status-label lookup). test-dispatch-dedup-stale-{no-worker,pagination,terminal-evidence}, test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-open-pr, test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation: all pass. test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh: 2 claim-POST stderr-file failures, identical on origin/main.

Resolves #34008

title: GH#34040: keep worker origin reachable and verify blocked-release commit durability
body:
## Summary

Fixes both defects in #34040.

**Defect 1: the worker network policy sometimes denied the dispatched origin.** Every retained denial was `network.worker-policy` → `git-push-destination-missing` for a bare `git push`. A bare push/fetch/pull resolves its default remote through two git queries with a 5 s hard timeout. Any failed or slow query turned into an anonymous denial. An explicit `git push origin <branch>` was always allowed.

- `command_policy_network.py`: the git queries now get 2 attempts with a configurable timeout (`AIDEVOPS_GIT_POLICY_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default 10 s, range 1–60). `_run_git_query_detailed` returns a failure token: `timeout`, `spawn-error` or `exit-N`.
- `command_policy_git.py`: the current branch is read with plumbing (`git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD`) instead of porcelain.
  - If only the branch query fails, the analyzer classifies every remote a default lookup could select (origin plus configured branch/push remotes). Each one still goes through the tier policy. This replaces the denial.
  - A remaining denial names the step that failed, e.g. `git-push-destination-missing(config-query-timeout)`.
- `network-tier-helper.sh`: `check_argv` denials now end with `[layer=… rule=…]` and are written to the denied-access log (`log_policy_denial`), so each denial can be traced to a layer and rule.

**Defect 2: the blocked-release (`permission_required`) path said work was preserved, but unpushed commits were lost.** Cleanup only unregisters the worktree. The exit-time push fallback archived a diff, which is empty for work that is already committed.

- `headless-runtime-failure.sh`:
  - New `_worker_secure_branch_commits` checks whether any commits are unreachable from `origin`. If so, it pushes the branch. If the push fails, it writes a git bundle under the dirty-worktree archive root and checks it with `git bundle verify`. If both fail, it returns `work_lost`.
  - `_push_wip_commits_on_exit` now falls back to the same bundle when its push fails.
- `headless-runtime-worker.sh`: `_hrw_finish_permission_required_run` runs that check and archives uncommitted edits before posting the handoff. On `work_lost` it also writes a blocker-log entry. It passes `--durability` to the helper.
- `worker-permission-helper.sh`: the hard-coded "The worktree and OpenCode session are preserved" line is gone. The comment now shows what the runtime actually verified: pushed, bundled (with a home-normalized path), no unpushed commits, `work_lost`, or "not verified". The signed request envelope and request ID do not change.

## Testing

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh`: 223 of 224 pass, including a new test that injects query failures (branch-query failure uses the superset, an unsafe superset is labelled, a config failure is labelled, a timeout is retried). The one failure is `interactive sessions keep signing overrides available`: it sees the headless-worker environment of this run, not the code changed here.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exit-classifier.sh`: 29/29, including a new test using disposable repos that covers none, pushed, bundled (bundle `list-heads` contains the branch) and `work_lost` (exit code 1).
- `test-worker-permission-helper.sh`, `test-permission-grant-verification.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-failure-classification.sh`, `test-worker-network-egress.sh` (12/12): pass.
- Every token was rendered through `permission_durability_text` and checked.
- `shellcheck` on all edited shell files: clean. `python3 -m py_compile` on the edited Python modules: clean. Pre-commit ratchets: pass.

## Qlty follow-up

The first head (`77f5b14`) added 2 `qlty:file-complexity` smells. `879a63f` moves the git query runner into `command_policy_git_query.py` and default-remote resolution into `command_policy_git_default_remote.py`; behaviour is unchanged. Local `qlty smells` now reports no complexity findings for these four files. The similar-code finding in `command_policy_git.py` was already on main.

## Scope note

`worker-permission-helper.sh` and `tests/test-worker-exit-classifier.sh` are outside the issue's persisted Files Scope. The false preservation claim is in the helper's comment template, so fixing Defect 2 required editing it.

Resolves #34040

title: GH#33891: fix: recover worker Git discovery and local CLI PATH
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #33891. Repair worker executable-discovery gaps without broadening network permissions.

- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_git_query.py`: prefer executable Git from the trusted NixOS system profile for fixed, local read-only remote queries, before conventional system locations. A failing `/usr/bin/git` guard alias previously made a valid `origin` appear unclassified. Preserve upstream's two bounded attempts and configurable timeout; failed queries still return no destination and do not retry through alternate transports. Actual Git mutations remain guarded.
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_evaluation.py`: resolve executable Bash from fixed NixOS and conventional system paths when invoking the network guard. Do not use worker-controlled PATH entries; unavailable Bash and timeouts remain fail-closed without transport fallback.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/runtime-path.mjs`: append an existing `~/.local/bin` so shell tools and plugin subprocesses can find the installed `aidevops` CLI, while preserving framework-guard and project-tool precedence.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-network.py`: cover NixOS precedence, `/usr/bin/git`, `/bin/git`, PATH fallback, non-executable candidates, fail-closed exit/error/timeout behavior, and actual local fetch/push URL resolution.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-shell-env-origin.mjs`: cover local CLI path recovery and make existing full-PATH assertions account for appended host profiles.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-linters-local-{changed-mode,complexity-gates}.sh`: repair existing test executable assumptions exposed by the upstream merge, retaining each assertion and explicit Git override support.

Commit `9af0055df` incorporates current upstream query extraction, resolves the conflict, and repairs the real-Git test's B603/B607 findings using an absolute executable and narrowly documented B603 suppressions for fixed, fixture-only subprocess calls.

Follow-up commit `f753bc95f` repairs a second live executable-path failure: seven recent worker attempts exited 126, and an installed-policy-only probe reproduced `network.helper-error` because `/bin/bash` does not exist on the NixOS host. `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bash` is executable. After scoped setup deployment, the same installed policy admits the classified GitHub remote and still forbids an unknown remote; no Git transport is executed by these probes. Setup reconciled Pulse onto the activated bundle.

## Observed failure and local verification

The policy's remote resolver returned no result for an existing worker worktree even though guarded `git remote get-url --all origin` resolved correctly. The hardcoded `/usr/bin/git` query exited 1 in that execution environment. Separately, a worker reported `spawn aidevops ENOENT`; the runtime PATH helper did not restore the directory containing the CLI.

After a scoped atomic local runtime deployment:

- The deployed worker-policy checker admits the intended GitHub remote for read and push commands. These are policy-only checks; no branch was pushed by the probes.
- An unknown remote is still forbidden by `network.worker-policy`.
- The deployed runtime PATH starts `aidevops secret status` from a restricted base PATH. Probe output is limited to spawn and exit status; no secret values or authentication artifacts are recorded.
- The existing headless worker canary exits successfully; this is not evidence of a fresh completed worker delivery.

## Verification

```text
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-network.py
  11 tests passed
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-shell-env-origin.mjs
  20 tests passed
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main
  All changed-file gates passed, including secretlint
git diff --check
  Passed
Pre-push repository verification
  bun run typecheck passed
```

### Cross-distribution runtime evidence

The expanded Python suite passes on the NixOS host and in actual disposable Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 12 containers: **11 tests per environment**, including Bash system-path precedence and missing-executable/timeout denial. The unchanged shell-environment suite previously passed all 20 tests in each environment. The real-Git test initializes a session-owned temporary repository and resolves distinct configured fetch and push URLs without contacting either remote. Git setup fails the test if unavailable; this is not a skipped or mocked integration assertion.

Final verification also passes on both container distributions:

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh`: 224 checks, zero failures, including 41 offline SSH binding fixtures
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-linters-local-changed-mode.sh`: 28 assertions passed
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-linters-local-complexity-gates.sh`: 26 assertions passed
- `bandit -q -t B603,B607 .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-network.py .agents/scripts/command_policy_evaluation.py`: no findings for the reported subprocess rules

Both linter test suites also pass on the NixOS host. Containers use read-only source mounts, no injected host credentials, a container-owned temporary directory, and automatic removal. Required tools are installed from each image's configured distribution repositories. Final runs use the locally available `ubuntu:24.04` and `debian:bookworm-slim` images. Initial container failures from missing temporary-directory setup and `jq` were resolved by providing those prerequisites, without weakening assertions.

Head `9af0055df` passed CodeFactor, Codacy, Qlty, SonarCloud, Ubuntu setup/CLI lifecycle, Linux systemd smoke, and Ubuntu 22.04 verifier-boundary checks. Four jobs were still running at the follow-up inspection, with no completed failures and a successful replacement for a cancelled maintainer-gate run. Fresh CI for `f753bc95f` must be evaluated independently; prior CI success is not claimed for the new head.

Other Linux distributions have executable-layout regression coverage, not a claim of actual Fedora/Arch/Alpine runtime validation. Container evidence verifies the repaired discovery and shell-environment modules, not complete authenticated workers or scheduler/service behavior on each distribution. No new CI matrix or runner infrastructure is added.

## Scope and limitations

This PR does not remove publication/review holds, bypass untrusted-brief checks, disable source-access safeguards, reset API budgets, or claim that the entire worker fleet is healthy. Local pulse resumed candidate evaluation, but no fresh successful worker delivery was verified. Queue/trust holds and GitHub REST-evidence deferrals remain separate diagnostics.

The repair is installed locally as a hotfix. Upstream merge and a subsequent framework update are still needed for durable distribution. No release or auto-merge is requested.

title: fix(pulse): associate non-closing worker issue references
body:
## Summary

Separate worker PR task association from issue-closing authority. A downstream managed repository repeatedly skipped clean, non-draft worker PRs with `pm-wb-no-issue` even though their bodies explicitly declared a non-closing `For #NNN` reference.

The root cause is the closing-only body resolver feeding the worker-authority gate. Empty GitHub `closingIssuesReferences` metadata is expected for partial deliveries and is not the underlying parser dependency. The Linked Issue Check has a different policy, including trusted-author exemptions, so its success does not prove Pulse resolved a task identity.

No source-repository tracking issue was assigned to this interactive request; no issue number or task ID is inferred from a title.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`: extend the existing `_extract_pr_work_issue` helper with explicit-reference mode and use it locally in worker merge gates. Preserve `_extract_linked_issue` and all post-merge closing behavior.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh`: resolve the same non-closing association at the final boundary so live linked-issue NMR still blocks.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`: require the referenced number to resolve to an actual local issue, not a PR or unavailable metadata, before applying the existing issue-author trust chain.
- Existing regression suites under `.agents/scripts/tests/`: extend extract-linked-issue, worker-briefed, admin-safety-check and issue-sync-authority coverage.

Standalone local `For #NNN` / `Ref #NNN` declarations can identify partial deliveries without authorizing closure. Title-only IDs, incidental prose, quoted/code/comment examples, cross-repository references and references in secondary-work sections do not supply a primary merge association. Distinct primary declarations fail closed. Existing closing targets remain authoritative and ambiguous closing targets do not fall back.

PR-author/worker-origin validation, draft/hold, required-check, review, requested-changes, NMR, security, migration, data-loss and final merge gates remain intact. No worker scheduling, concurrency, CI or installation changes.

## Verification

Run from the source worktree:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-admin-safety-check.sh

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

- Changed-file local gate passed: ShellCheck, Secretlint, whitespace, repeated-string regression, Bash 3.2 compatibility, portability, function-complexity and nesting-depth checks. Formatting differences remain advisory and were also present on the untouched base; no broad reformat was performed.
- Four focused suites passed: 29 + 25 + 27 + 10 = 91 assertions.
- The partial-delivery regression reaches the real worker-authority gate without the no-linked-issue skip, retains an empty closing target, and remains blocked when the review gate fails.
- Final-boundary coverage confirms primary issue scoping, live NMR blocking and rejection of unapproved external-worker authority.
- Adjacent parent-close, partial-parent, role, interactive and required-check suites passed.
- Two adjacent suites failed identically on untouched base commit `814201d9152e1b69d69be38373f7b67715790891`: `test-pulse-merge-carry-forward-diff.sh` (2 fence assertions) and `test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh` (11 failures involving the missing extracted `_route_pr_resolve_work_issue` dependency). Those unrelated defects are not changed here.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: merge-authority association change. Verification level: focused offline gate/association regressions plus read-only live PR and issue metadata inspection, not an installed operational fix.

Direct shell evaluation of source resolver functions against live PR bodies was blocked by command policy. No live merge-capable processor was invoked to test parsing. No existing PR was merged, no issue was closed, and no automation was deployed or installed.

## Review-only authority and rollout

This PR is intentionally draft and carries `hold-for-review`. The maintainer authorized committing, pushing and opening a PR only. Do not mark ready, remove the hold, merge, release or install without separate authorization.

After review and explicit rollout authorization, publish through the normal aidevops process and install the reviewed source revision with `bash ./setup.sh --non-interactive`, or use `aidevops update` after a release containing the fix. A fresh Pulse process must load the updated installed scripts, and operational diagnostics must then verify the no-issue skip disappears while other gates still apply.

title: t18631: GH#34146 deny protected reads and notify local-only failures
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34146. For #34125.

- Deny unbound Read/Grep/Glob/list and Bash/bounded-operation reads of operator-classified protected roots before tools, provenance resolution or intent logging run.
- Retain the frozen Phase 1 binding. Bound reads remain subject to existing source/secret permissions.
- On bound local HTTP 404, refused connection, timeout, model-identity mismatch or policy denial, emit one content-free foreground toast and bounded receipt per session per 30 seconds. Headless/no-TUI sessions retain receipts.
- Reject shell option execution, quote concatenation, newline chaining, opaque interpreters and path aliases; preserve unclassified native reads.

## Files and reference patterns

`private-processing-policy.mjs` implements frozen root classification, the pre-execution gate and the local stop notification, following existing read/toast patterns. `quality-hooks.mjs` applies the gate at the shared V1/V2 boundary. `provider-error-diagnostics.mjs` delegates local failure events; `local-only-policy.mjs` exports content-free error classification without changing egress. `v2.mjs` adds event wiring. Two synthetic test files and the private-AI/binding docs cover the behavior. Phase 1 request semantics and Phase 3 egress surfaces are unchanged.

## Classification decision

Use operator-owned `local-only-roots.json` in the aidevops user config directory (mode 600, current-user-owned regular file, absolute roots), frozen at plugin startup. Every root has the strict local-LLM-only processing label. This is classification, not a new authorization store. Vault's storage helper does not expose a path-to-processing-label registry; operators must register plaintext roots explicitly. A missing list preserves unclassified reads; malformed or insecure configuration fails closed.

With configured roots, unbound shell reads permit only a single literal, option-free reader. Opaque programs cannot safely be classified and are denied. No model output, tool argument, later environment change or on-disk edit can replace the active policy snapshot. Trusted future restarts remain a new launch trust decision.

## Readiness decision

Reuse the frozen local-only binding and Phase 1 provider/loopback request checks. Do not add a network probe: a successful local parent turn demonstrates availability, not service attestation; a probe cannot establish that the loopback service will not forward data. Host session-error handling stops the failed turn; notifications never authorize remote fallback.

## Independent security review

[Independent review result and repaired findings](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/34155#issuecomment-6085713072): sign-off for the stated current-launch boundary. The same independent reviewer confirmed the final complexity-only helper extractions do not weaken the reviewed boundary.

Residual assumptions: trusted same-process plugins and shell/executable resolution, bounded argv execution, no adversarial filesystem alias races; descendant symlink traversal depends on host tool behavior. This is not an OS sandbox. Bound Bash remains unchanged. The V2 compatibility client currently exposes no TUI API, so its failure events produce durable receipts without a foreground toast; unavailable TUI never clears a stop.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Level: runtime-verified. Final implementation head: `3be6e013a`.

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-private-processing-policy.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-local-only-policy.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-error-diagnostics.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-source-access-guidance.mjs
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
markdownlint-cli2 .agents/reference/vault-local-only-binding.md .agents/private-local-ai.md
```

- 37/37 scoped tests pass under Node v24.21.0. Real plugin factory children use only synthetic data, proving denied reads never expose the sentinel and later environment changes cannot clear the binding. Existing sentinel tests prove no simulated external send from bound sessions.
- Changed-file checks pass; direct Markdown lint reports zero issues on both edited docs. The bounded linter PATH did not locate the globally installed Markdown CLI, so it was invoked directly from the discovered executable.
- Push-hook `bun run typecheck` passes. Existing oversized-document and secret-policy warnings are baseline debt, not regressions.
- The security reviewer inspected code and assertions independently; it did not claim test execution or access private data.
- Terminal Qlty and CodeFactor complexity findings on the previous head were repaired by extracting focused helpers. Local Qlty v0.652.0 reports zero smells across all three policy/error modules; CI uses pinned v0.643.0. No scanner suppression, threshold override or config change was applied. Remote reruns remain asynchronous.

title: t18632: GH#34147 gate local-only tool egress
body:
## Summary

For #34125. For #34147. Adds verified fail-closed tool-egress gates and records the remaining sandbox compatibility gap under the brief's safety-stop fallback. The parent must remain open; this PR does not claim arbitrary local shell/listener startup is supported.

## Files and reference pattern

- `local-only-policy.mjs`, quality hooks, image and MCP activation tools reuse the frozen launch binding and content-free denial.
- `config-hook.mjs` and `v2-mcp-adapter.mjs` snapshot trusted resolved MCP entries, rather than tool-supplied destinations. These necessary integration paths were recorded in the canonical issue scope before edits.
- Six content-sending helpers use `vault_runtime_policy_check`; shell environment and OTEL enrichment suppress bound telemetry.
- `opencode-launcher-helper.sh` disables OTEL before SDK startup and preserves the binding across conversation `env -i`. This necessary startup integration was also recorded in canonical scope before editing.
- Terminal CI repairs extract shell/tool policy and the Python bridge into `local-only-shell-policy.mjs`, `local-only-tool-policy.mjs` and `vault_runtime_policy.py`; all three were added to canonical scope before editing. The Python bridge uses fixed absolute Bash and fixed route labels, without shell evaluation or payload arguments; its scoped B603 annotation documents that reviewed fixed-argv false positive.

## Bash mechanism and residual risks

No command denylist is treated as a sandbox. Bound opaque commands, interpreters, env-cleared child commands and unknown tools fail closed. Only a literal `/usr/bin/curl --disable --noproxy '*' --proxy '' --max-time 30 --url 'http://127.0.0.1:PORT/path'` (or equivalent loopback URL/argv) is allowed; on NixOS the fixed trusted executable is `/run/current-system/sw/bin/curl`. No redirects, curlrc, proxy configuration or shell composition. Bounded-operation restoration commands are checked too. This deliberately restricts arbitrary local commands/listener startup until an OS sandbox is available. Already-running owned loopback listeners, native local file tools and trusted local MCP remain usable.

Plain `curl <literal-loopback-URL>` and its two-element argv are normalized to that safe execution form before the existing command-policy gates. Ordinary loopback calls therefore work without inheriting curlrc/proxy risk. The independent reviewer also inspected this final normalization and found no concrete injection or egress bypass.

title: t18617: fix(ci): bound replay and review monitoring job hangs
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33986 (t18617).

- Bound `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` job `model-replay-linux` to 20 minutes and its `Install Bubblewrap` step to 8 minutes.
- Bound `.github/workflows/code-review-monitoring.yml` job `code-review-monitoring` to 30 minutes.
- Preserve runners, permissions, conditions, and `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-replay-benchmark.mjs` unchanged. No optional adjacent job changes.

## Timeout evidence

Queried the latest 20 monitoring runs with `gh run list -w code-review-monitoring.yml -L 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,updatedAt,conclusion`, then fetched successful job start/end timestamps to exclude queue time. The 15 successful monitoring jobs lasted 88–833 seconds; nearest-rank p95 was 833 seconds (13m53s). Three times p95 rounds up to 42 minutes; the issue explicitly caps this timeout at 30, so use 30 minutes. The replay and apt step limits are the brief's specified values.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: low; testing level: self-assessed CI configuration.

- Both complete workflow files parsed successfully with installed `js-yaml`; assertions verified all three timeout values, the Ubuntu 22.04 hosted runner, and the unchanged replay boundary suite command.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Push hook `bun run typecheck`: passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/lint-workflows-helper.sh .github/workflows/code-quality.yml .github/workflows/code-review-monitoring.yml`: returned success but reported no installed linter; this is not semantic validation evidence. The independent YAML parse above supplies syntax validation.
- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-replay-benchmark.mjs`: cannot complete on this runner because Bubblewrap is absent. It rejects with `No enforcing verifier filesystem sandbox is available on linux`, before the expected prompt-guard failure assertion. No replay code was changed. Enforcing boundary verification remains on the PR's Ubuntu 22.04 job, which installs Bubblewrap.

## Regression Evidence

This is a three-line GitHub Actions timeout configuration fix, not a platform implementation change. Automated reproduction of GitHub-hosted apt mirror hangs and enforcement of the Actions scheduler's job timeout is not possible in a repository unit test without deliberately stalling external infrastructure for 8–30 minutes. Existing verification is retained rather than introducing a synthetic timeout harness: both complete workflow files parse, structural assertions check the exact 20/8/30-minute values and unchanged hosted runner and replay suite, and the existing Ubuntu 22.04 replay boundary job installs Bubblewrap and runs `test-model-replay-benchmark.mjs`. The PR's Code Quality Analysis and Code Review Monitoring runs provide live regression evidence. Local replay is limited by the absent enforcing sandbox, as recorded above; no test behavior or security guarantee has been relaxed.

## Remote acceptance

The exact-head Code Quality Analysis and Code Review Monitoring runs must complete successfully, with the replay boundary suite still executing. Pending checks are handed to Pulse; no remote success is claimed before terminal results.

title: t18640: feat(mcp): add SEO Utils MCP support via on-demand @seo-utils
body:
## Summary

Adds SEO Utils MCP support using the same on-demand pattern as PostHog, DataForSEO and Backblaze B2. The `seo-utils` MCP is registered globally disabled. Only the bounded `@seo-utils` agent connects it through `aidevops_mcp`, and it disconnects when the task is done.

- **Launcher** `.agents/scripts/seo-utils-mcp-launcher.sh`: finds the SEO Utils executable in `/Applications` or `~/Applications` on macOS, or uses `SEO_UTILS_BIN` on other systems. It runs `<bin> mcp-stdio` and needs no token or Node.js. It refuses to start builds that lack `mcp-stdio` (2.5.0 and earlier), because those builds ignore the argument and start the full app backend with its schedulers.
- **Registry**: new `seo-utils` entry with a 900000 ms `timeout`, because some SEO Utils actions run for minutes and OpenCode's default is 60 s. Generated local entries now carry an optional `timeout`. A user-owned entry, for example one created by SEO Utils "Add to OpenCode", is kept but stays disconnected.
- **Agent** `.agents/seo/seo-utils.md`: covers the tool model and the three action classes:
  - `read_action`: free
  - `lookup_action`: spends credits
  - `write_action`: needs approval for every call

  It also routes questions to local data before paid lookups and covers workspace scope, destructive and spend safety, setup for other runtimes and troubleshooting.
- **Template** `configs/mcp-templates/seo-utils.json`: entries for OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex and `mcpServers`-style clients.
- **Index wiring**: `seo.md`, `domain-index.md`, `mcp-integrations.md`, `subagent-index.toon` (regenerated with `LC_ALL=C`), capability registry, URL allowlist.

Resolves #34205

## Verification

- New `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-seo-utils-mcp-registry.mjs`: 4/4 pass. It covers the disabled entry and timeout, disconnecting a user-owned entry, restricting tools to `@seo-utils`, and the launcher running `mcp-stdio` only on supporting builds (via stub binaries).
- `shellcheck` on the launcher: clean.
- Launcher with the installed app: refuses to start and reports "no mcp-stdio server (2.5.0 or earlier)". A missing `SEO_UTILS_BIN` also fails closed. A stub binary receives `mcp-stdio`, and dry-run validates it.
- Registry probe:
  - The `seo-utils` entry is generated with `enabled:false` and `timeout:900000`, and the global `seo-utils_*` tool gate is `false`.
  - A user-owned entry is kept and forced to `enabled:false`.
  - The `@seo-utils` profile gets `seo-utils_*` + `aidevops_mcp`, and its prompt includes the agent doc.
- `node --test` `test-mcp-activation.mjs`, `test-posthog-mcp-registry.mjs`, `test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`: 54/55 pass. The one failure (`V1 tool definitions adapt to structured V2 registrations`, `schema.object is not a function`) also fails on `main` and is tracked by t18633 / #34148.
- `capability-readiness-helper.py check`: valid. markdownlint on the changed docs: 0 issues.

## Not verified

A live MCP handshake needs an SEO Utils build newer than 2.5.0 with the MCP add-on enabled. The installed build doesn't have `mcp-stdio`, so the launcher correctly refuses it.

title: GH#34293: docs: keep Qlty on organisation repos and skip its out-of-minutes check
body:
## What

Repository setup and management guidance now says what the merge tooling already does. On organisation (and private) repositories, Qlty's GitHub App runs out of minutes each month. The out-of-minutes "qlty check" is billing: skip it, keep the app, and never make it a required check.

- `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md` rule 14: the minutes return monthly, so keep the app installed (not a reason to remove Qlty); never require "qlty check" on a limited repository; points to `qlty.md`.
- `.agents/tools/code-review/qlty.md`: Quick Reference bullet and a "GitHub App: monthly minutes" section for setup and management. It covers keeping the app, skipping the failure, never requiring it, real findings still counting, and the split between the app's check and CLI-based CI gates. It names the helpers that already skip it (`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` `apply_qlty_billing_policy`, `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` `_pmrc_repo_has_qlty_credit_limit`).
- `.agents/tools/code-review/setup.md`: Qlty row in the platform table, the rule in one line, and a troubleshooting row for "out of minutes".
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-new.md`: an out-of-minutes qlty check still proves Qlty is connected; skip it, never remove Qlty.

Why: in an owner session, an agent read a red out-of-minutes qlty check as a reason to remove Qlty from an organisation. It edited four repositories' docs and asked the owner to uninstall the app, when the owner's policy is to keep it for the free monthly minutes. title: t18653: fix(pulse): resume reconcile single pass from a cursor after budget abort or stage timeout (GH#34299)
body:
## Summary

`reconcile_issues_single_pass` restarted at the first repository and first issue every cycle. Recent passes all end by time-budget abort (360s) or stage-timeout kill (380s), so every issue past the abort point was starved indefinitely. Concretely, parent #34125 has had 3/3 sub-issues closed since 2026-10-10T19:16Z but no pass reaches it. Sibling #34180, earlier in the scan order, closed about 294s into the 22:31 run, which was then killed at 22:38:00Z.

The pass now keeps a resume cursor, following the checkpoint pattern in `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh`.

Resolves #34299
Ref #34125

## Changes

- New `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-cursor.sh`, sourced by the orchestrator so the 1.7k-line file barely grows. It loads and validates the cursor (`slug<TAB>issue<TAB>attempts`), writes it with builtin `printf` (no fork per issue), clears it, rotates the slug list, and seeks to the cursor issue.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`:
  - Records the in-flight issue before its stages run, so a kill resumes there.
  - On a budget abort, records the next unprocessed issue or repo.
  - Rotates repos to start at the cursor repo and fast-forwards that repo's rows to the cursor issue.
  - Clears the cursor when the rotated list completes, so the next pass starts at the top and every issue is covered across cycles.
- Poison-pill guard: an issue resumed `AIDEVOPS_RECONCILE_SP_CURSOR_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 2) times without finishing is skipped and logged, so one slow issue cannot pin the cursor.
- A malformed cursor, an unknown repo, or a cursor issue that is no longer open falls back safely: original order, or the top of that repo.
- Cursor path override: `AIDEVOPS_RECONCILE_SP_CURSOR_FILE`. Default: `~/.aidevops/state/reconcile-single-pass.cursor`, alongside the existing `parent-repair-repo.cursor`.
- `tests/test-reconcile-budget-isolation.sh`: pins the cursor to its temp dir so test runs never touch the real state file.
- New `tests/test-reconcile-single-pass-cursor.sh`: drives the real orchestrator with stubbed stages that advance `SECONDS` to simulate cost. It covers abort → resume → rotation → completion → clear, kill-retry with attempt increment, poison-pill skip, and the fallback cases.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-reconcile-single-pass-cursor.sh` → 18 passed, 0 failed.
- Existing suites, all rc=0: `test-reconcile-budget-isolation` (7/7), `test-pulse-issue-reconcile` (37/37), `test-pulse-reconcile-parent-task-subissue-graph` (46/46), `test-pulse-parent-backfill` (12/12), `test-maintenance-selector-contract`, `test-pulse-labelless-reconcile`.

title: GH#34324: fix: throttle bounded-operation escaped-process marker scan to decision points
body:
## Summary

Periodic bounded-operation tracking ran a full process-environment scan (ps axeww on macOS, /proc/PID/environ on Linux) on every 250 ms tick to recover escaped marked processes (GH#33747), costing about 0.4 CPU cores per running operation on macOS. The scan now runs on the first track and at most every 5 s from periodic ticks (MARKER_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS), and is forced at command exit, in both termination passes (SIGTERM and SIGKILL), and before the drain loop reports a drained tree. The cheap parent-chain snapshot keeps its 250 ms cadence. Also adds the t18656 TODO entry and brief.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-tree.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18656-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Tracker measurement: 10 s at the 250 ms supervisor cadence with an operation ID, under /usr/bin/time -p, on a 16-core macOS host with about 960 processes. Before: 1.45 user + 2.54 sys = 3.99 CPU-s over 10.18 s (about 0.39 cores). After: 0.31 user + 1.06 sys = 1.37 CPU-s over 10.13 s (about 0.135 cores). With no marker scan at all the floor is about 0.11 cores. node --check passes on both modules. node --test test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs + test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs: 21/21 pass, covering GH#33514 nested groups, GH#33747 escaped servers on completion/cancel/expiry, GH#34047 post-exit receipts and PID-reuse identity. markdownlint is clean on TODO.md and the brief.

## Regression Evidence

- The change is platform-independent scheduling: it changes when the escaped-process marker scan runs, not how it scans. The macOS (`ps axeww`) and Linux (`/proc/PID/environ`) scan implementations are unchanged by this PR.
- The safety-relevant behaviour that now depends on forced scans is already covered by existing plugin regression tests: GH#33747 escaped servers recovered on completion, cancel and expiry; GH#33514 nested process groups; GH#34047 post-exit receipts and PID-reuse identity. `node --test` on `test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` and `test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs` passed 21/21 locally on macOS for both commits (`ad747d20b4`, `08dd8a1a0d`). These plugin tests do not currently run in CI, and the unchanged Linux `/proc` scan path was not re-run for this PR.
- The CPU reduction is deliberately not asserted by an automated test: CPU time on shared CI runners is nondeterministic, so a threshold assertion would be flaky. It was measured locally with `/usr/bin/time -p` (see Runtime Testing). A repeat measurement after the behaviour-preserving Qlty refactor (`08dd8a1a0d`), under heavier host load, gave 0.37 user + 1.44 sys CPU-s over 10.23 s for this branch versus 1.67 user + 2.74 sys CPU-s over 10.27 s for the canonical `main` checkout.

Resolves #34324

title: GH#34342: fix cost breaker double-counting resumed-session footers
body:
## Summary

Root cause: dispatch-dedup-cost.sh::_sum_issue_token_spend summed every worker signature footer, but gh-signature-helper-session.sh reports cumulative OpenCode session time and tokens. Continuation dispatches that resumed one session posted 89,214 -> 217,569 -> 356,637 (6m -> 6h 5m -> 13h 2m), so each later footer re-counted earlier spend and the window after the last detected checkpoint totalled 809,536 > 800,000 across 4 footers. Contributing gap: three merged For-#N checkpoint PRs had no timeline cross-reference events and no PARTIAL_PARENT_CLOSEOUT marker, only 'PR #N' prose in signed worker reports, so _cost_checkpoint_from_closeouts missed them. Fix: footers by the same author whose implied session start (created_at - duration, widened by display resolution plus 120s slack) overlaps and whose tokens do not decrease are chained as one session; only increments count, and a pre-window footer is the baseline. Footers without author/time/duration keep full counting. Up to three highest 'PR #N' mentions in trusted signed comments become REST-verified checkpoint candidates (same base-repo + For/Ref/Resolves + merged_at checks as closeouts); unreadable mentions are skipped, never fail-open. Budgets and breaker strength are unchanged. Read-only verification against the private original: before 809536|4; with session fix 502753|4; with both fixes 355184|3. title: t18663: fix(pulse): stop stale-blocked sweep and dep-graph refresh starving repos with real backlogs
body:
## Summary

Both periodic dependency-recovery stages now spend their budget on repos that still have work. Stale-blocked sweep: each repo records its own completion stamp after a clean, complete pass; repos with a fresh stamp are not re-listed, and the sweep budget is shared only among due repos (partial, failed or never swept). Unblock decisions (_der_try_unblock, _refresh_try_unblock_issue), cursors, batch limits, stage timeouts and the global sentinel are unchanged.

title: t18668: fix(pulse): restore footprint defer suppression for bodiless candidate snapshots
body:
## Summary

Footprint defer suppression now works with the candidate JSON that Pulse actually passes it. Candidate snapshots are listed without `body` (`pulse-repo-meta.sh`), and `.body // ""` turned that into an empty footprint. Every reconsideration therefore woke the defer with `candidate_footprint_changed` and re-ran the full candidate ceremony before re-deferring on the same blocker.

- A candidate JSON without `body` now reads the issue body. An unreadable candidate falls through to the live check without ending the defer.
- Local expiry is checked before any GitHub read.
- A blocker that became a `parent-task` or claimed `no-auto-dispatch` coordinator wakes the defer (`blocker_coordinator_recheck`), so the live check applies its coordinator exclusions.
- Each suppression logs `[footprint-defer] event=suppressed`, and `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` gains a `pfd-suppressed` rule.
- The default TTL rises from 1800 s to 21600 s; `AIDEVOPS_FOOTPRINT_DEFER_TTL_SECONDS` still overrides it.

Why: `pulse-stats.json` shows 681 footprint-overlap blocks and 0 suppressions. Over 66 h of `pulse.log`, 246 of the 297 `candidate_footprint_changed` wakes were re-deferred against the same blocker within 900 s (wake to re-defer p50 78 s, p90 147 s; 21,735 candidate-seconds). Deferred candidates came back at a median age of 10,593 s, so a 1800 s TTL covered 5% of reconsiderations; 21600 s covers 89%.

No dispatch, claim, dedup, trust or budget gate changes. Suppression only skips a candidate whose footprint is unchanged while its recorded blocker is still open, in flight, not a coordinator and unchanged, which the live check would defer again.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18668-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — local gates and a negative control; live check after deploy.
  - ShellCheck is clean.
  - `test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` 40/40 on Bash 5 and on `/bin/bash` 3.2. Five new production-shaped cases: bodiless snapshot suppresses, unreadable candidate falls through, fetched-body edit wakes, coordinator blocker wakes, expiry wakes without GitHub reads.
  - Negative control: the same suite against the origin/main module fails 4 of the 5 new cases. The bodiless-snapshot case wakes with `wake_reason=candidate_footprint_changed` at age 0, the live symptom.
  - `test-pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` 175/175.

Resolves #34373

title: t18583: read-only Hostinger fleet inventory, plan and drift check
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of t18583: a read-only Hostinger fleet **inventory**, **plan** and **drift** check (`hostinger-helper.sh fleet ...`), plus fleet-scoped `migrate-layout plan --source` selection.

Nothing in this PR mutates hosting, GitHub, repositories or `repos.json`. Provisioning, readiness verification and the layout-move wrapper are later phases (see "Remaining phases").

For #33811
Supersedes #34343 (its two checkpoint commits are cherry-picked here with authorship retained).

## What changed

- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet.py` (CLI), `hosting_fleet_inventory.py` (normalization), `hosting_fleet_plan.py` (classification), `hosting_fleet_remote.py` (API/SSH I/O):
  - `inventory`: fetches every page of `GET /api/hosting/v1/websites` and refuses a partial result. Groups sites by account document root into codebases (primary / network-member / alias). Optional `--discover-networks --ssh ALIAS` runs a fixed, read-only `wp core is-installed --network` / `wp site list` probe that adds multisite blogs with no panel entry. `--network-map` covers the case without SSH.
  - `plan` / `drift`: classify each site against `repos.json` and the shared owner-layout policy (`repo-discovery-lib.sh`) as `ok`, `ok-exception`, `new`, `unregistered-clone`, `missing-clone`, `misplaced`, `owner-mismatch`, `collision`, `ambiguous` or `not-in-hosting`. Plans and inventories are content-hashed; a tampered inventory is refused. `drift --fail-on-drift` exits 3 when there is drift.
  - Output goes to an owner-private `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/hostinger-fleet/` (0700 dir, 0600 files). The token comes from `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN` and the wrapper injects it via `aidevops secret`; it is never printed or written.
- `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`: `fleet` subcommand.
- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py`, `repo-layout-migrate-helper.sh`, `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`: `--source PATH` (repeatable) limits a layout plan to exact repositories. Consumer inventory and all apply guards still apply, and an empty selection is refused (from #34343).
- Docs: `services/hosting/hostinger.md` "Fleet inventory and drift"; `reference/repo-organization.md` `--source` note.

Module names avoid the `.gitignore` credential pattern `hostinger_*` instead of weakening it.

## Findings that shaped the design

- The Hostinger API edge returns HTTP 403 to Python urllib's default User-Agent, so the client sends an explicit one.
- The panel reported `website_type: other` for a live multisite network. Discovery therefore probes every `domains/*/public_html` root, and a probe result overrides the panel type.
- Multisite blogs with mapped domains have no panel entry. Without discovery they would show up as false `not-in-hosting` drift.

## Verification

- Live, read-only run against one authorized account: 23 panel entries, 29 sites after network discovery, 16 codebases, 3 multisite networks. Drift found 6 real items (3 new sites, 1 misplaced clone, 1 owner exception, 1 registration no longer hosted). Repeat runs produce the same `inventory_sha256`.
- Synthetic workspace exercising the `collision` and `not-in-hosting` states. Negative paths: invalid owner, malformed `DOMAIN=OWNER`, invalid SSH alias, missing token, tampered inventory hash.
- `python3 -m unittest tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`: 15 tests OK.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`: clean. `qlty smells` on all new and changed scripts: none. `markdownlint` on changed docs: clean.

## Remaining phases (tracked on #33811)

1. Provisioning with per-site receipts: private repo creation/adoption, native init, registration, resume and partial results.
2. Readiness verification: visibility, owner, default-branch heads, effective features, Pulse/maintenance flags, worker auth.
3. Fleet layout-move wrapper: snapshot and restore of maintenance and Pulse settings around `migrate-layout --source`.

title: t18669: fix(pulse): stop footprint extraction turning EDIT/NEW prose and template placeholders into shared file claims
body:
## Summary

Footprint extraction no longer turns `EDIT`/`NEW` prose or template placeholders into file claims. Pulse inlines the consolidation instructions into every consolidated issue, so each one claimed the same fake paths (`regressions.`, `path/to/file`, `todo/<area>/...`). An in-flight consolidated issue then deferred all the others, and prose such as "Inherited NEW wildcard lines" made `wildcard` a claim shared by unrelated issues.

- An `EDIT` or `NEW` marker without its colon now declares only a backtick- or quote-wrapped path (``- NEW `tests/x.mjs` ``). Before a bare word it is treated as prose.
- Tokens containing `<`, `>`, `{` or `}`, or starting `path/to/`, are template placeholders and are dropped.
- Every other declaration shape is unchanged: colon declarations anywhere on a line, combined (`NEW/EDIT:`), repeated, bold, numbered, `### File:` headings, globs and line qualifiers.

Why: of the 243 defer records on this runner since 2026-08-24, 28 deferrals rested only on such tokens and 6 more included one.

- 21 of the 28 are in a managed private repo. There, one in-review issue with an open PR is the recorded blocker of 6 deferrals through `wildcard`. In 4 of them `wildcard` was the candidate's only overlap with any in-flight issue; the other 2 also share real paths with other in-flight issues, because `_footprint_find_overlap` lists every overlapping path but names only the owner of the last match.
- At 14:35Z, 2 of that repo's 4 live deferrals were `wildcard`-only, with about 5.5 h of their 6 h TTL left.
- The other 7 are in this repo (`only`, `if`, `the`, `declarations`, `(conditional)`).

Defer records hash the extracted paths (`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:314`, `:357`). After deploy, a deferral that rested on a dropped token no longer matches its record, so it gets the live check on its next reconsideration instead of waiting out its TTL.

No dispatch, claim, dedup, trust or budget gate changes.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18669-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed. Local gates, a negative control, a brief-corpus comparison and a live-issue comparison; live check after deploy.
  - ShellCheck is clean.
  - `test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` passes 41/41 on Bash 5 and on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57. The new Test 6b feeds consolidation prose, quoted examples and placeholders, which yield nothing. It also feeds combined, repeated, bold, numbered, heading, glob and colon-less backticked declarations, which are all kept.
  - Negative control: the origin/main extractor returns the same 9 real Test 6b paths plus `wildcard`, `regressions.`, `JSON`, `path/to/file`, `{path/to/new-file}` and two `<area>` paths.
  - Corpus: over all 928 `todo/tasks/*-brief.md` files, origin/main yields 3131 brief/path pairs and this change 3075 (56 dropped, 0 added). Every dropped token is a prose word, a placeholder or a brace-expansion prefix that the old regex cut at its comma. A first, line-anchored version of this fix failed this check because it also dropped real declarations (combined markers, several per line, bold, headings), so the fix rejects only the two junk shapes.
  - Live issues: 28 of 446 open issues in the private repo change, and 1 of 50 across 8 other managed repos. Every removed token is prose or a placeholder; nothing is added.
  - `complexity-regression-helper.sh`: 0 new function-complexity, nesting-depth or bash32-compat violations.
  - Live check after deploy: `[footprint-defer] event=deferred` records stop listing word or placeholder tokens. The affected candidates should wake with `candidate_footprint_changed`, then dispatch or defer on real paths.

Resolves #34380

title: t18672: fix(worker-lifecycle): stop the fix-the-fixer log watcher deadlocking workers before model invocation
body:
## Summary

Workers dispatched for `fix-the-fixer` issues deadlocked before their model started. `_start_run_attempt_observers` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-attempt.sh:337`) captures the verbose lifecycle watcher's PID with command substitution. The backgrounded watcher inherited that stdout pipe, so the capture waited for the watcher, while the watcher waited for log lines from a model that only starts after the capture returns. Its loop exits (worker gone, timeout, all checkpoints) were only checked after a line arrived, so nothing released it.

Live evidence: a fix-the-fixer worker held a slot for over five hours at `pre_attempt_observers_start`; `lsof` showed the wrapper reading a pipe whose only writer was the watcher, whose `tail -F` followed a 0-byte worker log. A second fix-the-fixer dispatch wedged the same way until its exit trap recorded `worker_runtime_not_invoked`; the other 56 retained worker logs passed the stage. Cleanup also leaked the `tail -F` follower: one started 2026-10-03 was still running eight days later.

Changes in `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-verbose.sh`:

- Redirect the watcher subshell's stdout to `/dev/null`, so the PID capture returns immediately.
- Poll the log with `read -t` (`AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE_WATCH_POLL_SECONDS`, default 5), so worker exit and `AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE_WATCH_TIMEOUT` are enforced on a quiet log; a failed read re-polls only while the follower is alive.
- Start the follower through a `sh -c` shim that prints its own PID and then execs `tail -F`, and stop it on every exit path and from a TERM trap via the new `_verbose_lifecycle_stop_follower`.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-verbose.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18672-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Process-level probe of the real module using the production call shape (PID captured by command substitution with stderr discarded, wrapper under `set -euo pipefail`, poll 1s), run on macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 and Bash 5.3.20 at head 782a98dfb5, identical results:

- complete (four checkpoint lines appended): capture 0s; `worker.session_created`, `worker.tool_started`, `worker.commit_attempted`, `worker.push_attempted` emitted; watcher and follower exited.
- cleanup (`_cleanup_verbose_lifecycle_watcher`): capture 0s; watcher and follower exited.
- quiet (no output, watch timeout 3s): watcher and follower exited after the timeout.
- crash (wrapper exits immediately): watcher and follower exited.
- follower death (`tail` killed externally, wrapper alive, timeout 1800s): watcher exited within one poll, no spin.

The old module under the same harness never returned the capture until killed externally.

Checks: ShellCheck clean; `linters-local.sh --changed` passed (shfmt, ShellCheck, bash32-compat, function-complexity, nesting-depth, portability, secretlint, markdownlint); `test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh` 34/34; `verify-brief.sh todo/tasks/t18672-brief.md` 5/5. Independent fresh-context closeout review of evidence bundle sha256 79e124035da7…: clean, no findings. Post-deploy runtime proof: the next fix-the-fixer worker logs `post_attempt_observers_start` and starts its model.

Resolves #34393

title: t18583: fleet site-repo maps and private fleet config
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 groundwork for t18583: lets fleet plan and drift handle sites whose repository has a different name, and stores fleet decisions once instead of passing them on every run.

- `--site-repo HOSTED_DOMAIN=REPO` (repeatable): a hosted site is served by a repository with a different name. Example: a pre-launch review subdomain whose future production domain names the repository. Several hosts may map to one repository without being flagged as a `collision`. Mapped sites report `ok-exception` and carry `served_by`. The mapped repository is counted as hosted, so it is not reported as `not-in-hosting`.
- Optional owner-private config `~/.config/aidevops/hosting-fleet.json` with `owner`, `owner_exceptions`, `site_repos` and `ignore`. Flags add to it, and `--owner` overrides it. A missing file means no stored defaults. A symlink, non-regular file or group/world-readable file is refused.
- `--owner` is no longer required when the config supplies it.
- Help text and `services/hosting/hostinger.md` are updated.

Files: `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet.py`, `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_plan.py`, `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`, `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`.

title: GH#34434: fix(release): unblock dependency-free release pushes and reconcile-required lanes
body:
## Summary

Every release push has been blocked since #34412 enabled the repo-verify pre-push guard: it runs `bun run typecheck` in dependency-free release worktrees (`tsc: command not found`), so version-manager fails after signing the tag locally. That failure path writes lane phase `reconcile-required`, which `_full_loop_release_claim_preserved_tag` never accepted, so `aidevops release reconcile <pr>` exited 75 with no output and no later release could reserve the lane.

- #34434: the four release-tool pushes set `AIDEVOPS_PREPUSH_REPO_VERIFY=0` for that one command only: direct main+tags (`version-manager-git.sh` `push_changes`), protected recovery branch and preserved tag (`version-manager-protected-main.sh`), and the hotfix signal tag (`version-manager-release.sh`). They carry only version-file bumps, provenance merges and signed tags on top of CI-verified main; every other pre-push guard still runs. One `#aidevops:trust-boundary` rationale block lives in `version-manager-protected-main.sh`.
- #34433: `_full_loop_release_claim_preserved_tag` (`full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`) also accepts `reconcile-required` with `tag == null`, under the same proofs as `preparing`. A same-source reclaim deletes the fenced `reservation_contract`, so the claim now also accepts lineage verified by `_release_lane_resolve_reclaim_evidence` (the rule `release_lane_recover_dead_preparing` already applies) and records it in `preserved_tag_recovery.reservation_lineage`. title: t18583: read-only fleet readiness verification (fleet ready)
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of t18583 adds `hostinger-helper.sh fleet ready`, a read-only check of whether each fleet repository is configured for background work. It takes the same options as `fleet plan`. It writes nothing to GitHub, clones, `repos.json` or project config.

It checks each plan repository once, even when several hosts share it.

**Problems (block readiness):**

- A plan state that isn't clean.
- The remote is missing or inaccessible, public, archived, owned by another account, or lacks push permission.
- The default branch is missing on GitHub, or `origin/<default>` is missing locally.
- The clone is missing, or its `origin` is wrong.
- The project config is invalid, or a required feature (`planning`, `git_workflow`, `code_quality`) is explicitly `false` (a legacy opt-out).
- Pulse is off, maintenance is `false`, or the repo isn't registered.

**Warnings (don't block):**

- No admin permission.
- A stale local default ref.
- No `origin/HEAD`.
- Registry feature labels that the project config doesn't make effective.
- A missing local `.aidevops.json`. Native gates then use defaults and inferred verification, which isn't an opt-out. The output gives the `aidevops project-config restore <slug>` preview command.

`all_ready` is true only when every repository is ready and `gh` is authenticated, so a partial fleet can never produce an all-ready receipt. The result is labelled *configured* readiness. `--worker-evidence` adds each repository's latest merged `origin:worker` PR as separate evidence. The receipt is written to the private (0600) state directory as `readiness.json`, with `readiness_sha256`. `--fail-on-not-ready` exits 4.

New modules:

- `hosting_fleet_checks.py`: per-repository collectors.
- `hosting_fleet_ready.py`: aggregation, receipt and output.

Both stay below the qlty complexity threshold.

For #33811

## Verification

- Live, read-only, against the real fleet: 28/28 ready, `all_ready=True`, gh actor resolved. Warnings: `project-config-missing=28` and `local-default-ref-stale=1`. Exit 0 with `--fail-on-not-ready`. With `--worker-evidence`, 3 repositories show a recent merged worker PR. The receipt is 0600.
- Negative paths, using real GitHub GETs and synthetic local inputs:
  - A public repository under another owner gives `remote-not-private` and `remote-owner-mismatch`.
  - A non-existent repository gives `remote-missing-or-inaccessible`.
  - `code_quality: false` gives `feature-disabled:code_quality` plus `registry-features-not-effective`.
  - Invalid JSON gives `project-config-invalid`.
  - Pulse/maintenance off gives `pulse-disabled` and `maintenance-disabled`; no registration gives `not-registered`.
  - Two hosts mapping to one repository, one `misplaced`, give one repository with both domains, `plan-state:misplaced` and `all_ready=False`.
- `linters-local.sh --changed`: all checks passed (ShellCheck, secretlint, markdownlint, Python 3.9 annotations, complexity ratchets). `qlty smells` is clean on the three Python files.

## Finding

None of the 30 fleet clones has a local `.aidevops.json`. Workers still run, but explicit feature flags and verify commands are absent. Restoring them is a per-repository `aidevops project-config restore <slug> --apply`, which needs an attached terminal and typed confirmation, so it's left to the operator.

title: t18583: resumable fleet provisioning from a reviewed plan (fleet provision)
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of #33811: `hostinger-helper.sh fleet provision`, resumable provisioning from a reviewed fleet plan.

- **Preview by default.** Without `--apply` it makes only read-only GitHub/Git queries and writes nothing.
- **Apply is bound to the reviewed plan.** `--apply` requires the exact `--plan-sha256`, verifies the plan's content hash, and refuses a plan older than 24 hours or one that the current fleet config contradicts (owner, `ignore`, `site_repos` or `owner_exceptions` changed).
- **Ordered, idempotent steps** for each provisionable state: `new` → remote, clone, init, deliver; `unregistered-clone` → init, deliver; `missing-clone` → clone. Every step re-reads live state first, so a repeat run adopts finished work.
  - **remote**: adopts an existing private repo under the expected owner and refuses a public or foreign one; otherwise runs `gh repo create <owner>/<repo> --private --add-readme` in the workspace (the workspace-exempt form in `reference/gh-command-discipline.md`).
  - **clone**: runs `gh repo clone`; refuses a destination with a different `origin`.
  - **init**: runs native `aidevops init planning,git-workflow,code-quality` (commits in its own `chore/aidevops-init` linked worktree and registers the canonical path); refuses a slug registered elsewhere.
  - **deliver**: pushes the init branch and opens an issue and linked PR through `gh-write-helper.sh`. It **never merges**: the result is `pending` until the PR is merged through `full-loop-helper.sh merge`. A closed, unmerged init PR is a failure, never retried.
- **Explicit partial results.** Each repository is reported as `complete`, `pending`, `planned` or `failed`. Steps stop at the first failure or pending PR, `--apply` appends every step to a 0600 JSONL receipt, and any failure exits 5.

## Files

- New: `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_provision.py` (selection, plan binding, orchestration, receipt), `hosting_fleet_steps.py` (remote/clone/init), `hosting_fleet_deliver.py` (push + issue + PR, no merge)
- Changed: `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet.py` (CLI), `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh` (dispatch/help), `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` (docs), `todo/tasks/t18583-brief.md` (phase 2 marked complete)

## Verification

- Preview against a stale saved plan: an already-provisioned repository was detected as fully done at every step, including its merged init PR (resume/adoption path).
- After the plan was regenerated: 0 drift and nothing to provision, so no account mutation was needed or performed.
- Refusals checked: `--apply` without a hash, a wrong hash, an unknown `--site`, and stale-plan guards (the real stale plan was refused for `ignore, site_repos` changes; owner change and newly ignored/mapped sites were also refused; the current plan was accepted).

title: t18583: fleet layout-move wrapper with automation snapshot/restore (fleet move)
body:
## Summary

Phase 4, the final phase of #33811: `hostinger-helper.sh fleet move`, a fleet layout-move wrapper around native `migrate-layout` that snapshots and restores automation. It also adds the native `aidevops repos pulse on|off` command needed to restore Pulse exactly.

- **Scope is explicit.** Every site must be named with `--site`. Unknown sites, and sites that are not `misplaced`, are refused, and whole-fleet moves are not allowed.
- **Preview is read-only.** It prints each move, the current maintenance/Pulse flags and the fleet plan hash, and writes nothing.
- **Apply** (`--apply --confirm <fleet plan hash>`):
  1. Recomputes the plan and refuses a different hash.
  2. Records each repository's flags once in an owner-private snapshot (0600).
  3. Pauses each repository with `aidevops repos maintenance off`, which also disables Pulse.
  4. Writes the scoped native plan (`--source ... --include-registered-paths`) **after** pausing, because the native plan records `repos.json` as a consumer before-state; pausing after planning makes native apply refuse with consumer drift. It refuses the plan unless its moves match the fleet moves exactly.
  5. Runs native apply with live output and no wrapper timeout (killing a journaled move mid-step is unsafe).
  6. Restores by slug with `maintenance on`, then `pulse on` (`maintenance on` alone leaves Pulse off), and reads both flags back as proof.
- **Failure handling:** a refusal or failure before anything moved restores automation and exits 6. A partial move stays paused, and the wrapper prints the native resume command and `fleet move --restore <snapshot>`; restore refuses unless every move or none happened. A new apply is refused while an unfinished snapshot covers the same repositories, so paused flags are never recorded as the originals.
- **`aidevops repos pulse on|off`:** a locked, atomic registry update following the `set_repo_maintenance` pattern. `on` is refused while maintenance is paused, which preserves the documented invariant that dormant repositories are never Pulse-eligible. Other fields are preserved.

## Files

- New: `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_move.py` (selection, native plan/apply, outcome), `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_automation.py` (flags, snapshot, pause/restore through the CLI)
- Changed: `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet.py`, `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`, `aidevops.sh` (`repos pulse`), `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh` (`set_repo_pulse`), `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`, `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`, `todo/tasks/t18583-brief.md` (phase 4 marked complete)

## Verification

- An isolated sandbox (temporary HOME, one registered misplaced repository with Pulse on) exercised the real native helper:
  - **Success:** native apply completed, the repository moved, the registry path was retargeted, `maintenance`/`pulse` were restored and read back, unrelated fields were preserved, the snapshot is 0600, preview wrote nothing, and a second restore was refused.
  - **Native plan mismatch after pause:** refused with nothing moved, and both flags were restored.
  - **Unfinished snapshot:** a new apply covering the same repository was refused.
  - The first sandbox run caught the ordering bug described in step 4 above (plan-before-pause), and the design was corrected.
- `aidevops repos pulse`, in an isolated registry: `on` refused while paused; `on`/`off` succeed with maintenance on; bad state and unknown slug rejected; other fields preserved. The existing `tests/test-repo-maintenance-state.sh` passes.
- Live, read-only refusals: no `--site`, an unknown site, a non-misplaced site, and a wrong `--confirm`.
- `qlty smells` clean, `shellcheck` clean, `markdownlint-cli2` 0 issues, `py_compile` OK, push typecheck passed, and zero matches against the private-term list.
- Not exercised live: no fleet site is currently `misplaced` (drift is 0), and any real move needs fresh operator authority.

Resolves #33811

title: t18675: fix(pulse): stop setup reconciliation killing in-flight Pulse cycles on every deploy
body:
## Summary

Setup's reconcile-managed no longer TERM/KILLs a launchd-managed Pulse cycle still running from an earlier runtime bundle. The cycle and its process tree finish on their own leased bundle and launchd starts the activated bundle from the stable link when the cycle exits. Cycles at or above a drain ceiling (default 3600s), a disabled drain (AIDEVOPS_PULSE_RECONCILE_DRAIN=0), an unloaded supervisor, or no running cycle keep immediate replacement. Standalone merge routines (stable-link launchd job, no bundle lease) are still retired while a cycle drains.
