title: t18680: fix(pulse): stop counting the async post-dispatch housekeeping run as a Pulse cycle
body:
## Summary

The async post-dispatch housekeeping run (GH#33256) outlives its cycle with PPID 1, its own process group and the bare wrapper argv, so `_pulse_pids` counted it as a main cycle. Setup reconciliation (t18675) measured the drain ceiling against it, so a housekeeping run past 3600s would make a deploy kill a young activated-bundle cycle, and `is-running`/`status` reported a running Pulse when no cycle ran (masking watchdog revival). The async run now writes an `async-pid` marker naming its executing shell (Bash 3.2 safe: `BASHPID`, else the `exec sh -c` `$PPID` pattern from `pulse-logging.sh`); the lifecycle helper excludes only that live PID from the main-cycle set (PID reuse guarded by marker mtime versus process start), defers a no-cycle reconcile for a young run, replaces one at or above the ceiling as before, and lists it separately in `status`. On Bash 3.2 the lock previously recorded the cycle PID, so the next cycle reclaimed a live run's lock and started a duplicate; it now records the async subshell.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18680-brief.md

title: GH#34480: publish protected repository metrics through one deterministic PR
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34480.

- Route a terminal metrics-push GH006 through one owned `aidevops/repository-metrics` branch/PR. Later refreshes replace only the generated snapshot with an explicit expected-head lease. Unprotected repositories retain direct publication; unrelated failures remain failures.
- Keep the job token as the first PR API principal, recover partial/concurrent creation before one bounded `SYNC_PAT` fallback, and explain missing PR permissions rather than presenting PATs as protection bypasses.
- Publish through a temporary index: preserve checkout HEAD, caller staging and unrelated paths. Reject stale scans, foreign branch ownership, extra branch history, non-ancestor snapshots, symlinks and path traversal.
- Update caller/reusable permissions and the existing SYNC_PAT detector/docs for metrics-only callers, including custom filenames.

## Files and Reference Pattern

- `.agents/scripts/repo-metrics-git-push-helper.sh`: metrics-specific publisher; follows `issue-sync-git-push-helper.sh` job-token-first PR creation/recovery/PAT and deterministic-branch patterns without importing TODO merge machinery or widening planning-publisher scopes.
- `.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml`, `.agents/templates/workflows/loc-badge-caller.yml`: publisher wiring and matching permission ceiling.
- `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper-repo.sh`, `tests/test-sync-pat-detection.sh`: preserve protection/Actions-permission advisory semantics and recognize active metrics `uses:` lines.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-metrics-git-push-helper.sh`: production publisher exercised against disposable real Git remotes; only PR API adapters are stubbed.
- `.agents/aidevops/badges.md`, `.agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md`: credential, PR lifecycle, permissions and upgrade guidance.

## Decisions and Compatibility

- No change to branch protection, administrator enforcement, maintainer approval, required checks or automatic merge policy. Success after fallback means a PR candidate is queued, not merged.
- Branch commits omit `[skip ci]`; the eventual squash title retains it for existing loop prevention. `GITHUB_TOKEN`-created events can still suppress Actions triggers, so consumer-required checks must execute through their authorized mechanism before merge.
- Existing callers must refresh `actions: read`, `contents: write`, and `pull-requests: write` permissions along with the reusable revision. Secret pass-through and explicit helper-ref overrides remain supported.
- **Required same-workflow repair:** actionlint 1.7.12 rejected the pre-existing `job.workflow_repository`/`job.workflow_sha` contexts on both baseline and changed YAML. Preserve helper pinning through the supported run API's exact `referenced_workflows[].sha`, with scoped `actions: read`; fail closed on missing/ambiguous provenance rather than drift to `main`. Live run API output confirmed these reference records, and tests execute the actual resolver shell from YAML.
- Preserve `fail_on_push_error: false` as the compatibility opt-out; do not hide failures by default.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk Level:** Critical (credential selection and protected publication).
- **Testing Level:** runtime-verified.
- Executed the production publisher against real local Git remotes. A receive hook rejects protected-default publication with GH006; PR adapters model permitted/disabled creation and partial success. No real token values or live branch-protection changes were used.
- Coverage: unprotected direct push, protected fallback, repeated branch/PR replacement, refreshed source base, custom/spaced paths and legacy output, preservation of staged/unrelated content, refusal to discard extra history, bounded PAT fallback, partial-success recovery, non-GH006 failure, warning-only mode, stale-source rejection and actual YAML helper-ref resolution.
- Limitation: this is not a reproduction on the reporter's private repository, nor a live `GITHUB_TOKEN`/PAT permission test. Native GitHub event suppression is explicitly documented rather than asserted away.

## Verification

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-metrics-git-push-helper.sh` | 30 assertions passed |
| `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-pat-detection.sh` | 28 assertions passed |
| `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-metrics-helper.sh` | 12 baseline assertions passed; generator unchanged |
| `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-reusable-workflow-permission-contracts.sh` | All 16 contracts passed |
| `shellcheck` on the four changed shell files | Clean |
| `bash .agents/scripts/lint-workflows-helper.sh .github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml .agents/templates/workflows/loc-badge-caller.yml` | Both valid with actionlint |
| `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main` | All local gates passed |

## Acceptance Self-Check

| Criterion | Result / evidence |
|---|---|
| Protected metrics publication has one deterministic PR; second refresh reuses it | Satisfied in real-Git runtime tests with GH006 rejection and PR adapters |
| Disabled Actions PR creation without PAT fails with permission-specific diagnostics | Satisfied in production publisher runtime test |
| Correctly configured PAT is a bounded PR API fallback, not a default-branch bypass | Satisfied by selected-principal runtime tests and unchanged protection path |
| Unprotected direct publication remains successful | Satisfied in real-Git runtime test |
| Diagnostics and documentation no longer blame absence of a bypass PAT | Satisfied by whole-file inspection and runtime error assertions |

- The profile-boundary fixture copies the worktree module family instead of maintaining another individual dependency list. Standard single-quoted SQL literals work with strict SQLite builds.

Give the deadline test enough startup budget to actually enter classification while retaining its six-second maximum and a longer blocking child.

title: feat(pulse): add repository-scoped GitHub App reads
body:
## Summary

Add opt-in GitHub App authentication for repository-scoped Pulse **reads**.
Recognized write operations, maintainer identity lookups and unscoped account
budget probes retain their existing auth path. Failed App reads never retry
with personal credentials. No production configuration or App permissions are
changed by this PR.

## Implementation

- Extend `aidevops repos pulse auth` with `set`, `status`, `check`, and `clear`.
  Store `pulse_auth` inside the existing repository registration without changing
  `pulse`, scheduling, or unrelated entries; reuse the registry lock convention.
- Add named profiles to the existing GitHub App config. Keep keys on the operator
  host and reject write permissions in Pulse profiles.
- Resolve read credentials at the gh shim boundary, before quota/REST routing.
  Require explicit repository context and isolate child gh credentials/config.
- Share JWT signing and installation-token exchange with the existing shell App
  helper. Keep Bearer credentials out of argv and HTTP diagnostic output.
- Restrict issued tokens to one repository; cache by App, installation,
  repository, permissions and key digest. Serialize refresh using a bounded,
  non-inheritable Python lock and renew before expiry.
- Document setup, compatibility, key rotation, rollback and unsupported scopes.

Primary implementation: `.agents/scripts/pulse_repo_auth.py`,
`.agents/scripts/github_app_auth.py`, `.agents/scripts/gh`,
`.agents/scripts/github-app-auth-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`,
and `aidevops.sh`. Existing reference pattern: the App helper and the
`aidevops repos pulse`/registry-lock lifecycle.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test_pulse_repo_auth.py`: 12 tests passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-github-app-auth-helper.sh`: 13 passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-rest-fallback.sh`: 105 passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-repos-help.sh`: passed.
- ShellCheck on all changed shell entrypoints: passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: passed; secretlint clean.
  Markdownlint was unavailable; the runner reports this as advisory, not as a
  completed Markdown lint. Existing shfmt formatting differences remain advisory.
- `test-gh-api-instrument.sh` passed its initial assertions but could not finish
  on this NixOS host: its native fixture forces `PATH` to `/usr/bin:/bin`, where
  bash is unavailable. This suite is **not** claimed green.
- Live isolated read-only POC against an operator-approved selected repository:
  native issue/PR reads and the real shared issue-list wrapper succeeded with an
  intentionally invalid personal credential in the parent. Direct REST returned
  401 after token revocation and the new shim failed; an invalid cached token and
  missing key also failed. Test tokens were revoked and temporary auth state was
  removed. No repository content, production Pulse config or App permissions
  were changed.

## Scope / review notes

This is the single-repository read-auth integration, not a full scheduler cutover
or a multi-host claim-coordination change. Additional permissions, account/bot
actor semantics, git transport and long-running worker refresh remain outside
this read-only scope. Multi-repository/unscoped repository reads and unknown gh
extensions fail closed rather than guessing an auth principal. Dynamic GraphQL
`--input` documents need explicit future classification.

Do not enable the setting across a production deployment before auditing its
remaining unscoped queries. Account-level budgets still describe the original
principal unless an explicit repository context selects an installation. Existing
response caches may return prior data without a new authorization request;
`auth check` uses a direct repository metadata API read rather than treating a
wrapper cache hit as proof of current authorization.

Rollback is explicit: `aidevops repos pulse auth clear OWNER/REPO`. It removes
only the per-repository selection, not tokens, permissions, or the Pulse flag.

title: GH#34538: fix(opencode): xAI Grok compaction targets 190K, below the 200K price band
body:
## Summary

xAI Grok now compacts at 190K usable input (limit.input 210K with the 20K reserve), below xAI's 200K long-context band. From a 200K prompt, xAI bills every token at 2x (docs.x.ai pricing; the OpenCode catalogue tiers also show size 200000). Root cause: Grok 4.5-4.7 catalogues advertise output equal to context (500K/500K), so the plugin computed zero input space and never capped them. OpenCode then compacted at context minus its 32K output clamp, about 468K, which matches the reporter's ~445K ledger. The OC1 budget now uses OpenCode's own threshold formula (context minus min(output, OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX) when no explicit input limit is set). The V2 adapter applies the clamp only to output>=context windows. There is a shared isXaiGrokModel matcher (xai provider, or grok- IDs on routers and clouds). Side effect: 324 of 8535 catalogue entries (Kimi K3, GLM-5.x, DeepSeek V4 and others) that GH#32807's documented 240K policy had silently skipped now get it. 262K/262K windows stay native.

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/context-budget-policy.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-limits.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-context-budget.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-v2-context-budget.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-context-budget.mjs, .agents/reference/context-efficiency.md, .agents/reference/settings.md, .agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md

body:
## Summary

Introduce explicit repository `github_auth.pulse.read/write` bindings and a unified `aidevops github auth` CLI. This is a read-only App rollout: reads support `github-app` or `inherit`, and writes support only `inherit`. App write routing is rejected rather than accidentally enabled by a new configuration shape.

- Add profile management in `github-auth.json`, explicit locked migration from flat `pulse_auth`, and clear errors for conflicting bindings or profile identities. Migration requires the operator to stop old Pulse processes and config writers; ordinary API calls never migrate configuration.
- Refactor configuration, policy validation, routing, runtime, migration and usage into `github_auth_*.py`. Keep thin compatibility entry points for existing callers and the shared `github_app_auth.py` token backend.
- Preserve interactive credentials and existing unscoped/unsupported routing. Once an App read is selected, it never retries with personal credentials. `check` refuses to report inherited transport as verified App access.
- Extend the existing telemetry format with optional consumer metadata; `usage --consumer pulse` filters recorded consumer values, excluding untagged historical rows. Reports remain local and are not GitHub quota or cross-host usage reports.
- Add `.agents/reference/github-auth.md` with App naming/ownership agreement, selected-repository installation, read-only permissions, key storage and rotation, CLI setup, migration and rollback. Update the existing App and registry references.

## Implementation context

Primary paths: `.agents/scripts/github_auth_{cli,config,policy,profiles,migration,routing,runtime,usage}.py`, `.agents/scripts/gh`, `.agents/scripts/gh-api-{instrument.sh,aggregate.awk}`, `aidevops.sh`, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test_pulse_repo_auth.py`.

Reference patterns: the existing mkdir registry lock, atomic JSON replacement, repository-scoped App token exchange, shared gh instrumentation, and current CLI module resolution. Existing Pulse booleans and scheduling fields are not changed. Old readers must not be left running against the migrated schema.

Independent advisory review findings were addressed: reject explicit null policies; share structural profile-document validation; detect legacy/canonical profile identity conflicts before migration. No lint thresholds or security gates were relaxed.

## Runtime Risk

Risk level: high. This touches credential selection, a persistent configuration format and shared request telemetry. App write permissions, bot-author trust, workflow dispatch and git transport changes are explicitly out of scope. No production deployment, scheduler restart or live registry migration was performed.

## Runtime Testing

Testing level: runtime-verified for the scoped read path; full instrumentation suite remains environment-limited.

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test_pulse_repo_auth.py`: 26 passed, including route isolation, unsupported App writes, explicit/idempotent migration, conflicts without partial registry writes, profile/CLI lifecycle, malformed input and consumer filtering.

A full suite pass is not claimed. Consumer filtering is additionally exercised through the real awk aggregator in the focused Python suite.

title: GH#34566: stop redacting public identifiers such as *_USERNAME
body:
## Problem

Exact-value redaction (GH#32362) treats every `export NAME=value` in `credentials.sh` as a secret, including public account identifiers such as `WPORG_USERNAME` and `SVN_USERNAME`. When the identifier equals the user's GitHub login, every GitHub URL, git remote and PR link in OpenCode tool output becomes `https://github.com/[redacted-credential]/...`.

Three paths leak identifiers into the redaction set:

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/registered-value-sources.mjs` `plaintextValues()` — all credential-file values plus env values for registered names.
- `.agents/scripts/redaction-digest-registry.py` `read_values()` — every record injected by `secret-helper.sh run`, so the identifier's HMAC is persisted.
- Existing digest registries already contain identifier digests and keep redacting even after the sources are fixed.

## Fix

- Names matching `(?:^|_)(?:USER|USERNAME|LOGIN|EMAIL)$` are identifiers, not secrets (`IDENTIFIER_ENV_NAME`, mirrored in the Python registry).
- The plugin excludes them from plaintext values and ignores digest matches for values held only by identifier names. A value also held by a secret name stays redacted.
- The registry stops registering identifier-named records.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-registered-value-redaction.mjs` (plus `test-credential-scrub.mjs`, `test-redacted-edit-guard.mjs`) pass.
- Fixture with `WPORG_USERNAME`, a `*_TOKEN` value and a pre-existing username digest: the username survives in a GitHub URL; the token and the digest-only value are still redacted.
- `redaction-digest-registry.py register` with a USERNAME record and a TOKEN record stores 1 entry.

Resolves #34566

title: GH#34605: fix(pulse): multi-runner-safe closed-issue receipts, write fuse, token-independent trust
body:
## Summary

Makes the Pulse feedback finalizer safe when several runners (servers and/or accounts) run at once and when reads use the GitHub App installation token. Under that token, org members' comments come back as `CONTRIBUTOR`.

Resolves #34605

## Changes (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh`)

- **Trust no longer depends on the reading token** (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`):
  - New `_feedback_route_author_trusted <repo> <login> <association>` accepts `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` as before.
  - Any other association is checked through the existing cached `_is_collaborator_author` (admin/maintain/write).
  - Result codes: 0 trusted, 1 untrusted, 2 unknown. Callers treat unknown as untrusted (fail closed).
  - `_feedback_route_trusted_entries` filters JSON comment summaries and caches one verdict per author per call.
  - It is the reusable building block for a future k-of-n quorum. That quorum is a non-goal here.
- **`_feedback_route_owner_allows`** and **`_feedback_route_release_comments`** use the new helper instead of `author_association` in jq. If a claim author's authority cannot be verified, the PR stays fenced (fail closed). The unused `PULSE_FEEDBACK_ROUTE_TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS` constant is removed.
- **Fleet-wide closed-issue receipt**: a receipt from any verified writer counts, so all runners share one comment.
  - This runner's own comments are matched by numeric `user.id` from `gh api user`, so no permission lookup is needed for them.
  - The marker core must be followed by ` -->` (legacy form) or `:RUNNER` (new form). This stops a SHA prefix from matching a longer SHA.
- **Writer identity**: `_feedback_route_authenticated_identity` returns `<id>\t<login>`.
  - It clears `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_REPO`, so `gh api user` stays unscoped and keeps the write credential instead of being routed to the App token (`github_auth_routing.py`).
  - If the identity cannot be resolved, nothing is written.
- **Convergence**: the oldest verified receipt wins. Each runner deletes only its own later copies, at most 20 per call.
- **Local write fuse**: after a successful comment, a file is created at `${AIDEVOPS_PULSE_FEEDBACK_FUSE_DIR:-~/.aidevops/state/pulse-feedback-route-fuse}/closed-issue-<repo_PR_ISSUE_SHA>`.
  - If the fuse exists but GitHub doesn't show the receipt, the runner logs it and applies the hold label without posting again.
  - So even when the read-back never finds the comment, each runner posts at most once per PR/issue/head.
- **`RUNNER:<id>` marker field** for diagnostics only. It is `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_RUNNER_ID`, or a `cksum` of the host name, so no host details are published. It is never used for trust.

## Verification

All passed locally:
- `test-pulse-merge-closed-issue-route.sh`. New cases:
  - Non-writer/impostor copy does not suppress.
  - Own CONTRIBUTOR receipt needs no lookup.
  - Another runner's receipt suppresses.
  - Permission failure plus an invisible receipt still gives exactly 1 comment (fuse).
  - Concurrent receipts: only our own duplicate is deleted.
  - Unresolved identity: no writes.
- `test-integration-recovery.sh`. New owner-allow cases: write collaborator seen as CONTRIBUTOR fences; permission lookup failure fences.
- `test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch.sh` (52 tests).
- `test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh` (72 tests).
- `test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh`, `test-pulse-residual-rest-reads.sh`, `test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh`, `test-ci-failure-pattern-detection.sh`, `test-conflict-pattern-detection.sh`, `test-gh-graphql-page-bounds.sh`.
- `shellcheck` is clean on all changed files. The `write_request` SC2120 warning in `test-integration-recovery.sh` that was already there is also fixed.

Unrelated failure: `test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh` fails 11/24 on base `87f6ed824` too, because `_route_pr_resolve_work_issue` is not in its awk extraction list. This PR does not touch it.

## Scope notes

- `test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch*.sh` did not need changes. Their release fixtures use positive associations, so no permission lookup happens.
- Non-goals, as agreed on #34605: signatures and quorum.

title: GH#34615: fix owned Playwriter relay group teardown
body:
## Summary

Ref #34615

Contributor draft implementing the reviewed owned-relay shutdown plan in the canonical launcher, with conservative recovery boundaries. This is not a claim that the issue's fresh-OpenCode runtime acceptance is complete.

- Put launcher-owned relay and MCP package runners in separate supervised POSIX process groups; terminate the groups concurrently with a 750ms TERM grace and KILL escalation, including descendants surviving runner exit. Neither child is unreferenced.
- Install persistent, idempotent SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers before startup and abort pending authentication probes on cancellation. Keep handlers installed through cleanup.
- Persist relay ownership before readiness polling, recording the process birth identity. Reconcile stale private marked state before probing or treating a relay as externally owned.
- Require private same-user regular files/directories, the exact state schema/host/port/version, a dead supervisor, a matching recorded birth identity, group leadership, and the reviewed package command before stale-group termination. Never signal based on port ownership.
- Preserve the reviewed 0.8.0 pin, environment-only token handling, version/token challenges, loopback binding, inherited MCP stdio, explicit browser-tab boundaries, and telemetry opt-out. No browser interaction was performed.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`: `spawnRelay`, `reconcileOwnedRelays`, and `supervise`; retains the existing private runtime marker and cleanup pattern.
- `.agents/scripts/lib/playwriter-relay-lifecycle.mjs`: extracts bounded group termination and conservative stale-runtime reconciliation into a focused module; the launcher supplies its unchanged ownership and reviewed-command contract.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`: extends the existing Node test file. No dependencies, new runner, activation adapter changes, or deployment changes.

## Reproduction and verification — 2026-10-14, macOS

The synthetic reviewed-command fixture starts a package-runner-shaped process plus an actual localhost listener on an OS-selected ephemeral port. The single-PID regression demonstrates that SIGTERM removes the runner while its TERM-ignoring descendant keeps listening; group termination then removes the listener and runnable descendant. Tests record PID/PPID/PGID/command topology without credential values. Supervisor tests run the production `main` path with only test-process fetch destination redirection to the ephemeral listener; they never bind or contact port 19988.

Commands and results:

```text
node --check .agents/scripts/lib/playwriter-relay-lifecycle.mjs
node --check .agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs
node --check .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs
  PASS
node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs
  PASS: 17 tests
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs
  PASS: 32 tests
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-pin.sh
  PASS: pin, updater, attribution, and extension-QA contracts
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main
  PASS: exit 0, including changed-file Secretlint and whitespace checks
git diff --check
  PASS
```

Lifecycle coverage includes stdio EOF/explicit exit; repeated INT/TERM/HUP; concurrent cleanup under the 2s host grace; cancellation during a hanging startup probe; restart after forced supervisor death with a still-identifiable relay runner; missing/mismatched birth identity; unsafe/symlinked evidence; live supervisors; and preservation of an external authenticated listener. Existing activation tests retain the registry handshake/command contract; the synthetic stdio exchange is not a real Playwriter handshake.

One independent supplied-source defect review identified two ownership/recovery defects in the first draft. Both were reproduced with failing focused tests, repaired, and included in the 17 passing tests. The subsequent bounded source review found no additional concrete P0/P1/P2 defect in the supplied source. That review predates the lifecycle-module extraction; it did not independently execute the tests or verify a live runtime. After extraction, all 49 lifecycle/activation tests, the Playwriter pin checks, and changed-file linters passed locally. Remote quality gates must still validate the new commit.

## Explicit limitations / maintainer decisions

- **Fresh OpenCode acceptance remains pending.** No installed launcher/configuration change, real Playwriter package run, live browser control, or existing relay replacement was authorized or performed. A separate authorized operator session must verify the maintained MCP connect/disconnect path, token enforcement, and actual owned-listener/state cleanup.
- **Unknown ownership fails closed.** Legacy state lacking a recorded birth identity, or a leaderless group surviving a supervisor SIGKILL during teardown, is preserved and reported as a startup failure rather than killed or silently reclassified as external. This patch does not claim complete automatic recovery for those cases. A stronger descendant-identity recovery contract would require further reviewed implementation; port-based cleanup is not acceptable.
- Forced supervisor death can also leave its MCP child; automatic stale reconciliation here is deliberately scoped to the relay. The forced-death fixture explicitly cleans its own synthetic MCP orphan.
- Real npx/bun behavior and Linux execution remain unverified locally. Synthetic process title/topology tests are not proof of the exact OpenCode kill path observed in the report.
- `needs-maintainer-review` was present when preparing this contribution. No approval label, signed approval, dispatch, or merge authority is changed or claimed.

Keeping `Ref #34615` avoids prematurely closing an issue with pending runtime acceptance and explicit recovery limitations. Rollback is a revert of this three-file change; no installation or live-state migration accompanies the PR.

The documented sudoers rule used an argument wildcard ([1-9]*). sudo-rs, the default sudo on Ubuntu 25.10+/26.04 LTS, rejects wildcards in command arguments (src/sudoers/tokens.rs:225-229) and ignores the line, so the opt-in privileged CWD inspector never runs and guarded cleanup stays cwd-visibility-degraded. The example now grants the executable with no argument list, which both sudo.ws and sudo-rs treat as any arguments (sudo-rs tokens.rs:198-200). This is security-equivalent: the wildcard already matched non-digit strings, and worktree-cwd-inspect.py main() requires root euid, exactly one [1-9][0-9]* PID and SUDO_UID, and same-user UID fields. The doc warns against argument patterns and "" and adds visudo -c -f validation plus sudo-rs detection.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Docs-only (self-assessed). Verified sudo-rs parser semantics from upstream source: wildcard args rejected; empty arg list allows any arguments; "" allows none. Verified the inspector's argv/SUDO_UID validation at worktree-cwd-inspect.py:44-51. markdownlint clean. Not runnable on this macOS host; reporter supplied the exact sudo-rs parse error from Ubuntu 26.04.

Resolves #34621

title: GH#34630: prove stale Playwriter guardian argv and process identity
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34630.

- Replace stale guardian substring checks with the exact Node executable, launcher path, guardian flag, and validated reviewed package-runner argv.
- Capture the guardian process-start identity before the asynchronous readiness probe, persist it in v2 state, and require it during stale reconciliation. Linux binds actual NUL-delimited argv to coherent stat snapshots and uses boot ID plus process-start ticks.
- Preserve older v2 state without an identity as unproven; retain legacy v1 exact-token reconciliation.

## Files and reference pattern

Only the three files in the issue's Files Scope are changed: the reconciliation module, authenticated launcher, and existing relay test module. Tests follow the existing synthetic process-group and marker-protected session patterns.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Testing level: runtime-verified. On exact head `226b01c3994499c887c972583a841b1b632c9c46`, `node --test --test-timeout=30000 .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` passes 10/10 on Node v22.23.3. All three changed modules pass `node --check`; `git diff --check` passes. The positive reconciliation test exercises the actual guardian launcher with a local npx stand-in and no network access. Negative tests preserve processes and state for substring impostors, mismatched/missing start identity, altered guardian tokens, and ambiguous ps argv. Legacy v1 reconciliation is covered.

`.agents/scripts/qlty-regression-helper.sh --base origin/main --head HEAD` passes on that exact head: 65 baseline smells, 65 head smells, delta 0 (Qlty 0.631.0). Push hooks pass repository typecheck and pre-push quality validation.

## Decisions and closeout review

- Older v2 state without an identity remains unproven while its group is live.
- Non-Linux ps does not expose trustworthy argv boundaries. V2 automatic stale termination deliberately fails closed there; normal guardian cleanup and legacy v1 compatibility remain unchanged.
- This hardening does not claim atomic pidfd-style signaling or extend legacy v1 identity guarantees.
- Independent final static review reports no actionable introduced defects. Acceptance review confirms exact v2 argv, coherent process-start identity, fail-safe preservation, legacy handling, and required negative coverage. All implementation edits stay within the canonical three-file scope.

Release notes

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's releases.

plugin-react@6.1.2

Fix HMR for compound components (#1484)

Adding or removing a component from a compound component was not handled, creating stale updates. Doing this now triggers hmr invalidate on the file and propagates the invalidation to importers.

Fix compiler.logDiagnostics option not working (#1483)

With oxc-transform-react >= 0.148, the logDiagnostics was not working. This version fixes it and requires oxc-transform-react >= 0.152 as a peer dependency if you are using the compiler option. compiler.logDiagnostics option is now deprecated and should be swapped for the builtin compiler.reportDiagnostics.

Disable refresh for non-jsx with compiler enabled (fix #1478) (#1485)

When the compiler was enabled, TS files could trigger fast refresh which would cause runtime errors. The logic now follows what the builtin oxc plugin in Vite does.

title: GH#34644: fix(dispatch): trust write-authorized CONTRIBUTOR/NONE authors via permission lookup
body:
## Summary

Private org members (including org admins) are reported by GitHub as author_association=CONTRIBUTOR/NONE. _gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority now routes CONTRIBUTOR and NONE through the same authenticated per-repository permission lookup as COLLABORATOR: admin/maintain/write is trusted, read/triage/none/404 stays untrusted, lookup failure stays rc=2. The installation-auth owner repair stays COLLABORATOR-only; FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR/FIRST_TIMER/MANNEQUIN remain untrusted without a lookup. _check_external_issue_author_gate now blocks without NMR mutation when the authority lookup is unavailable (matching Stage 0 reconcile) and logs failed NMR label writes instead of silently ignoring them, so the gate result and labels no longer disagree invisibly. The labelless backfill pre-filter in pulse-issue-reconcile.sh routes CONTRIBUTOR/NONE through the shared helper too.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-external-author-gate.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-gh-actor-authority.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: sourced the real shared-constants.sh + shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh and called _gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority against live GitHub for marcusquinn/aidevops: current runner (write) with CONTRIBUTOR -> rc=0 trusted-permission; with NONE -> rc=0 trusted-permission; outside user octocat with CONTRIBUTOR/NONE -> rc=1 insufficient-permission:read; octocat FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR -> rc=1 untrusted-association without a lookup. Suites: test-shared-gh-actor-authority.sh 17/17, test-pulse-dispatch-core-external-author-gate.sh 19/19, plus 14 related suites (labelless reconcile, external trust reconcile, NMR maintainer authority, full-loop external author gate, gh audit transitions, maintainer gate API failure, pulse-check-helper) all pass; shellcheck clean on all modified scripts.

title: GH#34646: fix: skip automatic updates for Nix-managed tools
body:
## Problem

On NixOS, `aidevops update` attempts to upgrade ripgrep using brew/apt-get/dnf/yum and fails with `No supported package manager found (brew/apt-get/dnf/yum)`. Ripgrep is installed and working from the Nix store (15.1.0). The updater should respect installation ownership rather than attempt an unrelated package manager.

## Implementation scope

- Modify `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh`: resolve installed binary symlinks and identify `/nix/store/` ownership before latest-version lookups or automatic update queueing.
- Represent Nix-owned tools as externally managed in console/JSON output, with no executable update command. Explain that users should update through the Nix configuration or profile that owns the tool.
- Never automatically invoke `nixos-rebuild`, Home Manager, or profile upgrades. Do not infer ownership merely from the presence of `nix`.
- Preserve existing update behavior for non-Nix binaries, including on hosts with Nix installed.
- Reference pattern: `check_tool`, `_print_tool_status`, `_output_summary_and_updates`, and existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-*.sh` checks.

## Acceptance and verification

- Nix-owned binaries (direct store paths and profile/system symlinks) receive an explicit externally-managed status, are excluded from automatic updates, and do not cause maintenance failure or false claims that an update was applied.
- Non-Nix tools retain existing classification and update routing.
- Run ShellCheck, bash syntax validation, existing tool-version regression checks, and the real `--category brew --update` and JSON paths on NixOS.

## Execution ownership

Requested by the operator for interactive implementation and assignment to their authenticated GitHub account. The primary interactive session owns implementation; no separate worker is needed while it is active.

## Delivery evidence

- Issue: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/34646, assigned to `vladimirdulov` and claimed for interactive implementation.
- Implementation was verified in the `bugfix/nix-managed-tool-updates` linked worktree. Deployment and release are outside this change's scope.
- ShellCheck, bash syntax validation, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Existing ripgrep, classification, update-failure, tap-formula, and OpenCode checks pass (OpenCode: 33 assertions). Classification coverage also exercises direct Nix ownership, symlink resolution, rejection of non-Nix/missing tools, skipped registry lookups, empty update queues, and honest summary wording.
- Real `tool-version-check.sh --category brew --update` succeeds on NixOS and skips jq/ripgrep. JSON reports `externally_managed` and an empty `update_cmd` for both.
- Existing `test-tool-version-check-brew-convergence.sh` exits 1 on both the implementation and unchanged canonical main. Its package-manager mocks do not change installed binary versions, while the updater requires verified version convergence. This is a separate baseline failure, not evidence of a Nix regression.

Resolves #34646

title: GH#34651: run the guarded Playwriter relay by default with a per-session token
body:
## Summary

Playwriter's guarded relay (GH#34615 process-group teardown) used to need OpenCode started as `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRITER_AUTHENTICATED_RELAY=1 aidevops secret PLAYWRITER_TOKEN -- opencode`. Normal starts got the plain command, and its upstream relay outlives disconnect. Playwriter is used occasionally by some users, so it should behave like every other on-demand MCP.

- `mcp-registry.mjs`: on macOS/Linux, framework-generated Playwriter commands are always wrapped in the guarded launcher; the environment flag is removed. Windows keeps the confined plain command because it has no process groups (fits #34629 / PR #34632, which makes the launcher refuse non-POSIX). Custom `mcp.playwriter` commands are untouched.
- `playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`: the opt-in gate is removed. The new `withRelayToken()` mints a random 64-hex per-session token unless a valid one (≥ 32 chars) was injected. The token reaches the guardian/relay and MCP child only through their environments. The guardian refuses to start without the supervisor's token, so it can never create a mismatched relay. When another session holds port 19988, the error now says what to do.
- Why no operator token is needed: in `playwriter@0.8.0` `cdp-relay.js`, the token is checked only on the client routes (`/cdp`, `/cli/*`, `/recording/*`). The extension's `/extension` WebSocket is gated by loopback address plus a known `chrome-extension://` origin.
- Test fix (pre-existing on `main`, macOS only): "preserves substring impostors…" applied the synthetic-guardian inspector to every session. On macOS `ps` splits the impostor's single argument into guardian-shaped tokens, so the helper forged argv proof and the impostor was reconciled. The production inspector never authorises v2 from `ps` output and kept it, as the first assertion shows. Linux CI reads `/proc` argv, so it passed there. The helper is now scoped to the iteration's own group, and the impostor is asserted alive in each iteration.

## Linked issue

Linked issue: Resolves #34651

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Runtime Testing

**Testing level**: `runtime-verified`

| Check | Result | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Dev environment started | pass | macOS arm64, Node 26.4.0, real `bun x playwriter@0.8.0`, command resolved through this branch's plugin with no flag and no `PLAYWRITER_TOKEN` |
| Smoke pages loaded | N/A | MCP `initialize` handshake completed (serverInfo `playwriter 0.8.0`) |
| Stability check (no reload loops) | pass | stdin-close and SIGTERM disconnects: no 19988 listener, process or runtime session dir at +0/+5/+15s |
| Key user flow | pass | Second concurrent session fails closed with the new message; the first session's relay is unaffected (same pid) and still tears down on disconnect. No 64-hex token in launcher argv or runtime files |

- `node --test --test-timeout=30000 .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`: 11 pass, 1 Linux-only skip.
- `node --test --test-timeout=60000 --test-reporter=dot .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`: pass.
- `biome ci` on changed JS and markdownlint on `playwriter.md`: clean.

**Escalation warnings**:

- [x] Changes environment variables or secrets handling

**Justification**: the token stays relay-scoped and loopback-only. The relay is now always token-protected, with a fresh random token per session instead of an optional long-lived one. It never appears in config, argv, state or logs (verified above). Upstream retitles `playwriter-serve`, and macOS `ps` then shows that process's environment to the same user. That is pre-existing upstream behaviour, identical with an injected token.

## Summary

Resolves #34652 (t18691).

Verified the previously unobserved LibreCrawl paths against upstream `05a1372de833` and clarified `.agents/seo/librecrawl.md`. All four behaviors work; no engine code changes are needed. Includes the start-URL/probe exception to URL filters, HTTP UA behavior with JS off, and timeout versus SIGINT export/cleanup behavior.

## Runtime Testing

Runtime-verified, low-risk docs-only change. Two sequential live passes against upstream `05a1372de8334ca18dec0bc1f7470c62901a9418`, Python 3.11 container. The WSGI listener was explicitly bound to `127.0.0.1:5055` using `serve(main.app, host="127.0.0.1", port=5055, threads=8)` with `LOCAL_MODE=true`. Host networking allowed the fixture and server to stay loopback-only; neither bound a network interface. The second pass used a loopback HTTP forwarding logger on port 5056 to observe API method/path/status without logging credentials. The fixture used relative links to three blog and three shop pages, or 360 slow linked pages (3 seconds per page) plus the start page. Temporary tooling was not committed. The fixture/proxy shut down and the owned LibreCrawl container was stopped after verification.

Each command below used this common prefix (output directories were separate per run):

```bash
LIBRECRAWL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5056 TMPDIR="$FIXTURE_TMP" \
  .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh crawl http://127.0.0.1:18765/ \
  --engine librecrawl --format csv --output "$RUN_OUTPUT"
```

|---|---|---|
| UA and normal regression: `--user-agent aidevops-ua-check/1.0 --max-urls 10` | 0 | `REQUEST / aidevops-ua-check/1.0`, `REQUEST /blog/0/ aidevops-ua-check/1.0`, same UA on robots and sitemap probes; seven CSV HTML rows; summary `complete: true`, `render_js: false`, `status: completed` |

| Timeout: `--timeout 1 --max-urls 1000` | 1 | Helper logged `Timeout after 1 min: stopping the crawl and exporting partial results`; API logged `POST /api/stop_crawl 200` followed by successful URL/link/issue exports; 99 CSV HTML rows out of 361 discovered pages; summary `complete: false`, `librecrawl.status: timeout`, `pages_crawled: 99`; same-session status after exit `completed` (not running) |

title: GH#34648: classify Playwriter relay extension state in mcp-diagnose
body:
## Summary

Playwriter 0.8.0 throws EXTENSION_NOT_CONNECTED_ERROR (relay-client.js:20-26) after a single local status probe (executor.js:695-707), and its text tells the agent to ask the user to click a gray icon. The aidevops activation guidance told the @playwriter agent to relay that diagnostic, so users with green tabs were repeatedly told to enable them. No aidevops tool read relay-side extension state.

- mcp-diagnose.sh playwriter now prints a classified 'Relay extension state' verdict: relay-down, relay-unresponsive, relay-version-mismatch, relay-up-no-extension, extension-rejected, extension-connected or extension-state-unknown. Evidence sources: loopback /version, a TCP check, /extensions/status (local extension count, enabled-tab count and versions only), the port listener's PID and process name (never argv, because serve --token carries a secret), and classified lines from the current relay run's ~/.playwriter/relay-server.log (truncated at each relay start). With the guarded relay's per-session token (default since #34655) the status endpoint returns 401, so the verdict comes from that log. If the configured command's version is unreadable (generated entries are disabled and wrapped at runtime), the expected relay version falls back to the reviewed pin in lib/mcp_config.py, so no new pin site is added.
- mcp-registry.mjs activationGuidance and playwriter.md (preflight step 3 and Troubleshooting) now direct the agent to run the diagnostic before disconnecting and report the verdict. They describe green-icon-plus-error as a browser/relay mismatch and never repeat the upstream 'click the icon' text.
- test-mcp-activation.mjs: the pinned guidance assertion is updated to the new contract.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs, .agents/scripts/mcp-diagnose.sh, .agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Real playwriter@0.8.0 relay on a private port: no token gives relay-up-no-extension, and a 403 unknown-extension handshake gives extension-rejected with the relay log line. With a per-session token the status endpoint is 401 and the verdict comes from the log; the diagnostic's own 401s are not counted. With serve --token in argv, no token appears in the full output. Listener is reported as PID:playwriter-serve. Fixture matrix covers all 7 verdicts, remote-extension exclusion, no profile email in output, control-character neutralising, and the reviewed-pin fallback (disabled bun x config plus a 0.5.0 relay on 19988 gives relay-version-mismatch). title: fix(release): classify explicit HTTP errors when ref headers are suppressed
body:
## Summary

Fix a release-recovery blocker discovered while refreshing the unpublished v3.39.31 aggregation for source PR #34603. `_release_lane_remote_head` currently drops stderr and relies only on an included HTTP header. The governed `gh` transport can suppress stdout on HTTP errors, so a verified missing successor branch is incorrectly classified as `unknown` after the lane has entered `aggregation-successor-preparing`.

Capture the response privately and recognize the CLI's explicit `(HTTP NNN)` status when no usable header is present. Only 404 means absent; 401/403, local cooldown, connection failures, and unknown responses remain blocked. Explicit 5xx retains existing retryable behavior. The helper never forwards response bodies or credentials.

Ref #34633

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh`: `_release_lane_remote_head`, retain header-based status handling with bounded explicit CLI-status fallback.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-lane.sh`: extend existing HTTP-classification regression with stderr-only 404, 401, 403, 503, cooldown, and unknown-response cases; no new test infrastructure.
- Reference: `.agents/reference/release-aggregation-recovery.md`, idempotent successor recovery and uncertainty handling.

## Runtime evidence

Installed CLI: gh 2.102.0 (nixpkgs). Native read-only `gh api --include --silent` returned `HTTP/2.0 404 Not Found` on the missing v3.39.31 tag ref. The deployed wrapper returned the same exit status and `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` on stderr but empty stdout. Disabling explicit pagination alone did not restore the header, so this fix does not disable pagination, API quota governance, authentication, write policies, or release provenance guards.

The original successor refresh persisted its fenced preparing checkpoint and then reported `Successor aggregation refused: branch identity is unavailable or malformed`. A maintainer subsequently completed successor #34662; it remains stale after newer main merges. This PR repairs classification only and does not publish, clear the lane, or rewrite any remote tag.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-lane.sh`: passed.
- `shfmt -d` on both files and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-lane.sh`: 23 tests, zero failures, including stderr-only status and fail-closed cases.
- Ordinary pre-commit validation and pre-push `bun run typecheck`: passed.

After required checks and review, merge this repair, refresh the latest stale aggregation at the exact new main tip, then resume the existing `recover-aggregate 34603` transaction with the complete verified source manifest. Publication and terminal receipts remain separate gates; no live publication is claimed here.

title: GH#34676: allow clones outside canonical checkouts
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34676.

- Classify clones from canonical checkouts by their explicit destination, accepting absent/empty paths outside canonical roots and registered separate Git metadata.
- Parse a conservative set of clone flags and value options; resolve successive relative `-C` options exactly once and follow symlinks before checking boundaries.
- Preserve protection for omitted, inside-checkout and non-empty destinations, unsafe auxiliary paths, and configuration/environment redirection.
- Explain blocked clones with the workspace-layout recovery guidance and document the allowance. Existing caller-side parent-directory workarounds remain unchanged.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`: narrow argv-checked exception alongside existing isolated-operation allowances.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_invocation.py`: explicit destination/auxiliary-path parser.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_shell_parser.py`: reject write/config environment overrides before assignments are discarded. This necessary integration was recorded in the issue's canonical Files Scope before editing.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`: requested regressions plus relative paths, symlinks, metadata and environment checks and a real shim clone.
- `.agents/reference/repo-organization.md`: documented behavior and conservative option boundary.

## Verification

Final verified head: `d3b3bd495b28cc431b34c5f8bdf6553973ebd64f`. Changed-file lint exits 0; the guard suite reports **172 tests, 171 passed, one unrelated pre-existing Nix failure** described below. All 29 new clone/credential checks pass. Pre-push `bun run typecheck` also passes. The exact-head immediate remote observation found no terminal failing checks; remaining CI was asynchronous.

- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --no-cache --base-ref origin/main`: changed-file gates, including ShellCheck, Markdown style, secret safety and Python annotation compatibility.
- `python3 -m py_compile .agents/scripts/canonical_git_invocation.py .agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py .agents/scripts/canonical_shell_parser.py`.
- `bash -n .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` and `git diff origin/main --check`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`: all added clone checks pass, including a real local clone through the PATH shim from a registered canonical fixture. The suite has one unrelated pre-existing failure on this Nix runner: its shared native/trusted-tool regression invokes `shutil.which("bash", path=os.defpath)`, which returns `None` because `os.defpath` is `/bin:/usr/bin`. The same lookup is present on the default branch; it then raises `TypeError` in `subprocess.run`. This existing behavior is deliberately not repaired in this task.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high (canonical Git write guard). Level: runtime-verified.

The existing integration suite executes the production shim and policy with native Git 2.54.0 and Python 3.13.15. It verifies successful outside cloning and preserved canonical refs/objects under blocked operations. A separate real `gh repo clone marcusquinn/aidevops <outside-destination> -- --depth 1` succeeded from a registered disposable canonical fixture through the production Git shim; `rev-parse --verify HEAD` returned `f36b376b1bcc96d02ba342576f75575816b400da`. The corresponding `git clone` without a destination remained blocked. GitHub CLI 2.102.0 injects credential-helper `-c` options: the allowance now validates their exact shell-safe grammar and root-controlled absolute `gh`/`.gh-wrapped` executable, while rejecting arbitrary helpers, shell controls and non-credential configuration.

## Review and acceptance

Independent focused security review identified object-directory redirection, separate metadata ancestry, and configuration-file selector gaps; each is addressed with rejection checks and scoped regressions. Successive `-C` resolution was checked against the actual `split_invocation` behavior (base cwd is retained, not pre-resolved). Direct final diff review confirms documentation, blocking guidance, requested clone cases, and unchanged caller workarounds. The guard remains a policy check, not a race-free filesystem sandbox.

title: GH#34675: LibreCrawl account sign-in and SEO Pro Stats crawl push
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34675.

- Add credential-safe LibreCrawl account sessions while retaining local guest sign-in.
- Add `push-seoprostats` and post-crawl uploads using inventory-based SSH/WP-CLI or authenticated REST imports.
- Prefer native LibreCrawl exports, enforce the plugin file limit, and bound REST job polling.

## Scope and reference

Changes are confined to the three site-crawler shell libraries/orchestrator and the two SEO guides listed in the issue. Contracts were checked against LibreCrawl's login and user-info routes and SEO Pro Stats' crawl import API, WP-CLI implementation and `docs/seo-loop-recipes.md`.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level**: critical (account credentials/session handling)
- **Testing level**: runtime-verified
- **Verified head**: `4725625b138093f2b66114378bf60b3bbb9d78ae`
- **Environment**: isolated, session-owned Docker services; LibreCrawl `05a1372de8334ca18dec0bc1f7470c62901a9418`, `LOCAL_MODE=false`, guest and registration disabled; WordPress **7.1.3**, PHP **8.3**, SEO Pro Stats **1.11.0** at `c590af0a14375aa13fd485d8968780b1e2b85cc8`. A second local-mode LibreCrawl instance verified the old guest-disabled autologin path.
- **Isolation detail**: rootless Docker cannot publish port 443. The REST check mapped the verified `127.0.0.1` TLS identity to the loopback high port using curl `--connect-to` and trusted only the disposable certificate with `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`; certificate validation was not disabled. SSH checks used a dedicated test key and a known-host entry obtained directly from the disposable server, with strict host-key checking. No production site or secret store was modified.

| Criterion | Evidence / result |
| --- | --- |
| Account login, session tier and crawl | Created and verified an extra-tier account using upstream `src/auth_db.py`; normal CLI crawl completed with **4 pages** and native exports. Local-mode guest-disabled autologin still returned admin. |
| Failed sign-in and credential safety | Wrong password failed with the account sign-in diagnostic, including in auto mode. A deceptive `localhost:5000@remote` HTTP authority was rejected before sending credentials. Process arguments and captured CLI output were checked throughout live account/REST calls: no password values. |
| Stored-secret fallback and unauthorized payload | Isolated shell contract checks exercised `aidevops secret get` fallback and verified the generated JSON body; an unauthorized response without a `success` field failed with the sign-in diagnostic. These two checks used a stub credential provider/API response, not the personal secret store. |
| REST native and mapped import | Multipart uploads and GET-driven import completion succeeded for raw LibreCrawl exports and for mapped CSVs; IDs and counts printed. `wp seoprostats crawl --format=json` confirmed **4 imported pages**. |
| REST negative paths and post-crawl flag | Real Application Password rejection returned HTTP 401/non-zero. A one-second import timeout returned non-zero while leaving server work intact. `crawl --push-seoprostats` then completed another crawl and REST import. |
| SSH native and mapped import | Automatic inventory-ready selection imported both file sets through real scp/SSH/WP-CLI. A deployment path containing a space and apostrophe worked. IDs/counts printed and no helper temporary directories remained. |
| SSH failure and upload limit | Invalid deployment path failed without REST fallback and still removed remote files. A 52,428,801-byte export was refused before transport execution. |
| Guides and CLI | Both scoped guides document account/shared/Cloudron use, transport choice, limits and exact secret naming. CLI help exposes the command and flag. |

Defensive malformed-response/job-ID/status handling, scheduler delay after sleeping, and cleanup-command failure were statically reviewed; they are not claimed as live server fault-injection tests.

## Local quality and review

- `bash -n` and `shfmt -d` on the three changed scripts: passed.
- `AIDEVOPS_PRE_COMMIT_BASE=origin/main git hook run pre-commit`: passed.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main`: **ALL LOCAL CHECKS PASSED**; ShellCheck **3 files, no warnings**, secretlint **5 files, no secrets**, Markdown style, Bash 3.2 compatibility, shell portability, complexity and nesting ratchets all passed.
- Push hooks: `bun run typecheck` and pre-push quality checks passed.
- Independent closeout review: two introduced transport edge cases were identified and repaired (loopback URL authority and post-sleep deadline); final review identified **no unresolved introduced defect**. Reviewed bundle SHA-256: `a90d6116323b05bcd1af39cb5ea48c1f45a5d7a9629502f9728d6af65a60599b`, prompt-injection scan clean. The host lacked `file(1)`, so bundle generation streamed only the requested artifact into the existing verification image's installed `file(1)`; no broad filesystem mount or installation was used.

Pre-existing/non-regressing observations: 19 oversized Markdown files (existing #21146), ten direct positional-parameter occurrences in the orchestrator, and existing LibreCrawl numeric-limit handling of leading-zero inputs. No unrelated repairs are included. Runtime setup initially encountered the expected rootless privileged-port limitation and Docker WordPress environment variables not reaching SSH; the disposable setup was corrected without changing host security settings or production code.

## Decisions and boundaries

- Keep guest/local behavior, but fail closed rather than silently changing engines after configured account authentication fails.
- Require HTTPS for account credentials except an exact HTTP loopback host; REST always verifies HTTPS and does not follow redirects.
- Prefer native exports, send one crawl's files together, and never retry through REST after an SSH write may have occurred.
- No scheduling or plugin modifications. New runtime artifacts remain outside the repository. Upstream changes were merged into the worker branch without force-pushing the early checkpoint.

title: GH#34681: fix worker blocker handoff classification and retained evidence
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34681. Continues the completed closed-issue label repair merged in #34683; no duplicate label implementation.

- Convert an unstructured `BLOCKED` exit into a post-PR handoff only when the existing verifier confirms an exact-head, linked, summarized, non-draft PR, the local worktree is clean, and the exact-head all-check observation succeeds or is pending. Explicit reasons (including unsupported reasons), failures and unreadable checks remain blocked.
- Capture final-assistant classification evidence before deleting transient output, using the existing credential-redacting, mode-600, size-bounded protected logger. Tool output is not accepted as assistant evidence.

title: t18695: Credential registry: record account, reach, owner, expiry and explicit provider defaults
body:
## Summary

Adds a non-secret local credential registry (~/.config/aidevops/credential-inventory.json, 0600). For each stored secret it records the provider, account (human name + ownership), reach (zones/resources), purpose, expiry and aliases. It also records explicit per-provider defaults, each one set, explicitly none, or undeclared. `aidevops secret` gains describe/record/account/default/alias/resolve (delegated to credential_inventory.py). `set` accepts --provider/--account/--purpose/--zones/--resources/--expires/--kind; these are validated before the value is read, so a rejection stores nothing. Also adds the TODO.md entries for the children of parent #34680. For #34680.

## Decisions

- The registry is stdlib Python (JSON handling) behind `secret-helper.sh` delegation, mirroring `hosting_fleet_*.py`.
- Raw account IDs are refused. `account_id_env` stores the name of the secret that holds the ID.
- A missing `defaults` key means undeclared and an explicit `null` means deliberately none, so consumers never infer a default.
- `.gitignore` gains a narrow exception for the placeholder template, which the `*credential*` pattern otherwise ignores.
- The registry code is split into four modules so each stays under the qlty `file-complexity` threshold: `credential_inventory_fields.py` (field rules), `_schema.py` (document validation), `_names.py` (defaults and aliases) and `_store.py` (I/O and records).
- `set` option parsing is extracted into `parse_set_options` to keep `cmd_set` under the 100-line function limit.
- Alias resolution at injection is deliberately left to #34718.

## Files Changed

.agents/configs/credential-inventory.json.txt, .agents/scripts/credential_inventory.py, .agents/scripts/credential_inventory_fields.py, .agents/scripts/credential_inventory_names.py, .agents/scripts/credential_inventory_schema.py, .agents/scripts/credential_inventory_store.py, .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh, .agents/tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md, .gitignore, TODO.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on the product path with an isolated HOME and plaintext fallback:
  - `set` with an unknown account is rejected before storing; credentials.sh is untouched.
  - `account add` followed by `set` with metadata stores the value and records the account.
  - The registry is written 0600 and contains no secret values.
  - `describe --json` returns account/reach/expiry/purpose offline.
  - `resolve` exits 4 (undeclared), then 3 (explicit none), then 0 (prints the name).

  - Re-run after the module split: identical output.

title: t18696: Credential aliases and explicit provider defaults resolve at secret injection

Stacked on #34726 (t18695 registry). Base is that branch, so this diff shows only the alias/default work; `full-loop-helper.sh merge` retargets it to `main` once #34726 merges.

When a requested secret name is **not itself stored**, `aidevops secret NAME -- CMD`, `run`, `get` and `check` now resolve it through the credential registry and inject the source value under the requested name, with output still redacted:

- **Declared alias** (`aidevops secret alias NAME OLD_NAME`) → the credential that declares it.
- **Provider conventional variable** (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `HCLOUD_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) → `defaults.<provider>`, **only when explicitly set**. Undeclared and explicit `--none` both leave the variable unavailable, as before.

title: t18697: aidevops secret dependents: show what uses a credential before rename, rotation or revocation
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34719. For #34680.

Stacked on #34732 (t18696), which is stacked on #34726 (t18695). Base is the #34732 branch, so this diff shows only the dependents work.

Adds `aidevops secret dependents NAME [--json]`: a local, read-only answer to "what uses this credential?" before a rename, rotation or revocation. It searches the name **and its declared aliases** (and works when given an alias).

| Source | How |
|--------|-----|
| Every repo in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` and all its linked worktrees | `git grep -F --untracked` (honours `.gitignore`), 30 s timeout per worktree, parallel |
| `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/` | bounded walk (5000 files) |
| `~/.config/aidevops/*.json\|conf\|toml\|yaml` (e.g. `site-inventory.json` `credential_env`) | file scan; the registry itself is excluded |
| `~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist` (binary plists decoded), `~/.config/systemd/user/*`, `crontab -l` | file/command scan |

Safety properties:

- **No values, no network**: it reads no secret store and outputs locations only (`path:line` and the matched *name*). Line text is used for classification and never returned, so values in scanned files cannot leak.
- **Never claims "unused" without evidence**: lines that build a name dynamically (`"CLOUDFLARE_${ACCOUNT}_API_TOKEN"`, concatenation, f-strings, `%s`/`.format`) are reported as `possible-dynamic` and set `complete: false`. Timeouts, truncation and unreadable files do the same. "No references found" is printed only for a complete, empty result.
- Literal matches are token-exact, so `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` does not match `CLOUDFLARE_ACME_API_TOKEN`.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_scan.py` (new): needle building, literal/dynamic classification, bounded `git grep`/file scanning; one subprocess site with an absolute executable (`# nosec B603`).
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_dependents.py` (new): source discovery (repos/worktrees, custom agents, configs, schedulers, crontab), report and text rendering.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_names.py`: `related_names` (canonical first, then aliases).
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory.py`: `dependents` subcommand.
- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`: dispatch and help line.
- `.agents/tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md`: Quick Reference rule ("run dependents before renaming/rotating/revoking; only trust `complete: true`") and a "Dependents" section.

## Verification

Isolated-`HOME` runtime script: two git repos (one with a linked worktree), custom agent, `site-inventory.json`, a binary LaunchAgent plist, and a canonical name plus an alias:

- Literal hits found in a tracked file, an untracked file, the linked worktree, the custom agent, the config (via the alias) and the binary plist; the gitignored file was not reported.
- `CLOUDFLARE_${ACCOUNT}_API_TOKEN` and `f"CLOUDFLARE_{acct}_API_TOKEN"` were reported as `possible-dynamic`, giving `complete: false` and an INCOMPLETE warning.
- A fake value placed on a matching line does not appear in the JSON output.
- After removing the dynamic lines, the result is `complete: true` with 7 literal hits.
- An unreferenced name prints "No references found in the scanned sources."
- Querying by alias returns the canonical name with its aliases.
- ShellCheck, `py_compile` and markdownlint are clean.

## Regression Evidence

This is not a platform fix. `systemd`, `cron` and LaunchAgent are mentioned only as read-only scan locations for a new command, and no platform-specific behaviour changes. No repository test was added: under the repo's test policy (`reference/ci-gate-policy.md`), the new feature was verified through the product path with an isolated-`HOME` runtime fixture (see Verification). That fixture covered a binary plist, linked worktrees, ignored and untracked files, dynamic name construction, and no value leakage. Existing `test-secret-helper.sh` passes 26/26.

title: t18698: Default-aware credential consumers: onboarding and MCP validation honour the declared provider default
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34720. For #34680.

Stacked on #34732 (t18696), which provides default injection. Base is the #34732 branch, so this diff shows only the consumer changes.

Onboarding and MCP validation no longer assume one unlabelled `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. When that variable is not exported, they read the credential registry:

| State | Onboarding status | MCP validation |
|-------|-------------------|----------------|
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` exported | `ready (API token configured)`, **unchanged** | existing test, **unchanged** |
| Default declared | `ready (default: NAME)` | connectivity test through `aidevops secret CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN -- ...` (default injection) against `/user/tokens/verify` |
| Tokens stored, no default declared | `partial (N stored, no default declared …)` (previously `needs-setup`) | warning that names `aidevops secret default cloudflare NAME` |
| Tokens stored, explicitly no default | `ready (N stored, explicitly no default)` | warning: tools must name an account-specific token |
| Nothing stored | `needs-setup` | warning |

- The count is registered `cloudflare` credentials plus stored-but-undescribed `CLOUDFLARE_*TOKEN|KEY` names, using names only.
- `onboarding-helper.sh json` keeps `hosting.cloudflare.configured` and adds `status` / `detail`.
- The Cloudflare setup guide no longer suggests storing a bare `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. It shows `account add`, `set CLOUDFLARE_<ACCOUNT>_API_TOKEN --provider cloudflare --account …` and an **optional** `secret default cloudflare NAME` (or `--none`). Onboarding never creates a default.
- The new connectivity test passes the bearer header to curl on stdin (`-H @-`), so the token never appears in any process argv.

- `.agents/scripts/onboarding-helper.sh`: `_cloudflare_status` / `_cloudflare_credential_count`, used by `status` and `json`; setup guide.
- `.agents/scripts/validate-mcp-integrations.sh`: `test_cloudflare_registry_default` for the not-exported path.

title: t18699: One credential naming convention; record account metadata at creation
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34721. For #34680.

Stacked on #34733 (t18697). Base is that branch because `credential-inventory.md` also changes there; this diff shows only the naming work.

The credential docs described five conflicting naming patterns and told readers to store the bare provider variable as the single-account default. There is now **one convention for new names**, defined once in `credential-inventory.md` "Naming new credentials"; every other credential doc points to it:

```text
<PROVIDER>_<ACCOUNT>[_<PURPOSE>]_<KIND>
```

- An account tag is used **even for the first and only account**, and the account is recorded at creation (`aidevops secret set NAME --provider P --account REF --purpose …`).
- The bare conventional variable (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) is never stored directly; it resolves only through an explicit `aidevops secret default`.
- The token label/value pair rule is kept as `KIND` suffixes (`…_TOKEN_NAME` / `…_ACCESS_TOKEN`), with `ORG` generalised to `ACCOUNT`.
- Provider dashboard token label: `aidevops-<account>-<purpose>`, recorded as the credential `purpose`.
- Existing names stay valid; renames go through `alias NEW OLD` plus `dependents`. Tool-mandated names (e.g. `OPENAI_IMAGE_API_KEY_<ALIAS>`) follow their tool's docs.

| Retired guidance | Where | Now |
|------------------|-------|-----|
| `<PROVIDER>_<KIND>_<ACCOUNT>` + "bare name is the single-account default" | `gopass.md` | pointer + account-tagged example with `--provider/--account` |
| `<PROVIDER>_<ORG>_<PURPOSE>_*` | `gopass.md`, `api-key-setup.md` | `<PROVIDER>_<ACCOUNT>_<PURPOSE>_*` |
| lowercase `-<account>` suffix; bare `openai-api-key` | `api-key-setup.md` | `hcloud-<project>-token`, `openai-<account>-api-key`; pointer |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN_PERSONAL` | `multi-tenant.md` | `GITHUB_PERSONAL_TOKEN`; pointer |
| `AI-Assistant-DevOps-[AccountName]` | `services/hosting/cloudflare.md` | `aidevops-<account>-<purpose>` stored as `CLOUDFLARE_<ACCOUNT>_API_TOKEN` |
| `HOSTING_SSH_PASSWORD_SHARED_ACCOUNT` | `configs/site-inventory.json.txt` | `HOSTINGER_SHARED_SSH_PASSWORD` (template only; no references) |
| `HCLOUD_TOKEN_{PROJECT}` | `services/hosting/hetzner.md` | new `HCLOUD_<PROJECT>_TOKEN`, legacy still valid |

**Small code change, required for consistency:** `onboarding-helper.sh` only detected `HCLOUD_TOKEN_*`, so Hetzner tokens named under the new convention would have shown as `needs-setup`. It now accepts both `HCLOUD_<PROJECT>_TOKEN` and legacy `HCLOUD_TOKEN_<PROJECT>`. The Hetzner setup guide now records the project and uses the new name. `hetzner.md` is outside the brief's file list, but it carried a conflicting convention.

Also fixes three pre-existing MD031 errors in `multi-tenant.md`.

## Verification

- `rg` over `.agents/tools/credentials`, `services/hosting/cloudflare.md`, `services/hosting/hetzner.md` and `configs/site-inventory.json.txt` for `<PROVIDER>_<KIND>_<ACCOUNT>`, `<PROVIDER>_<ORG>_`, `AI-Assistant-DevOps`, "remains the default for the single-account", "Naming with multiple accounts", `token-<project>` and `GITHUB_TOKEN_(PERSONAL|WORK)` returns no hits.
- markdownlint is clean on all 6 changed docs; ShellCheck is clean; `jq empty` passes on the template.

title: t18700: Cloudflare read-only verify, offline drift and owner lookup (GH#34722)
t18701: plan-first aidevops secret organise with unconfirmed drafts (GH#34723)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #34723. For #34680.

Stacked on #34741 (t18700). The base is that branch, so this diff shows only the organise work.

Cleaning up an inconsistent credential store is risky: renames silently disable features, and some consumers cannot be found by name. `aidevops secret organise` (alias `organize`) is a plan-first path that never renames, deletes, aliases or re-points anything. It combines the names-only `secret-helper.sh inventory`, the registry and the verification cache, and proposes:

- **Draft records** for undescribed secrets:
  - provider and kind come from a known name prefix and suffix;
  - an account tag that matches an existing `<provider>-<tag>` ref links that account; otherwise the tag is only a hint;
  - unrecognised names are listed for manual recording;
  - a stored bare conventional variable (e.g. `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) gets a draft plus a note.
- **Account refs from verified account names**, for recorded credentials whose verified token sees exactly one account.
- **Aliases instead of renames** for tokens with identical reach. It keeps the account-tagged, more-referenced name and lists the steps: dependents → move consumers → delete → `alias`. Overlapping reach gets a review note only.
- **A default decision per provider** whose default is undeclared: the candidate `default` commands plus `--none`.
- **A dependents count per credential** from one local scan over all names; `dependents NAME` remains the per-credential check before changes.

`--apply-drafts` writes only unconfirmed draft metadata:

- draft records for undescribed secrets;
- account refs from verified names;
- new accounts with `ownership.confirmed: false`.

Each written record carries `draft: {confirmed: false, evidence}` and shows `[draft, unconfirmed]` in `describe`. An explicit `aidevops secret record` clears the draft flag. Defaults, aliases, secret names and values are never written. Output is text or `--json`; `--no-dependents` skips the scan.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_organise.py` (new): proposals, dependents counts, `apply_drafts`.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_organise_infer.py` (new): name-based provider/kind/account-tag inference and drafts.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_organise_render.py` (new): text rendering. These are split out to keep each file under the qlty file-complexity threshold.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory.py`: `organise` subcommand; `record` clears `draft`.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_view.py`: `[draft, unconfirmed]` tag in `describe`. This file is outside the brief's list; the change is needed so drafts are visible.
- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`: dispatch and help line.
- `.agents/tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md`: Quick Reference pointer and an "Organise" section.

## Verification

Product path on an isolated `HOME` with a plaintext fallback `credentials.sh` holding 7 fake values. The fixture also had a verification-cache fixture (two tokens that see one account and identical zones) and a registered git repo that references them:

- `organise` / `--json` listed:
  - 4 drafts (`CF_STAGING_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACME_API_TOKEN` → existing `cloudflare-acme`, bare `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` with a note, `GITHUB_WORK_TOKEN`);
  - `MYSTERY_VALUE` as unrecognised;
  - `cloudflare-beta-co` account proposals from the verified name;
  - an alias proposal that keeps `CLOUDFLARE_NEW_DNS_TOKEN` (2 references) and retires `CLOUDFLARE_OLD_DNS_TOKEN` (1 reference);
  - default decisions for cloudflare (bare variable flagged) and github.
- `--apply-drafts` wrote 6 records and 1 account, every one `confirmed: false`:
  - `credentials.sh` SHA-256 is byte-identical before and after;
  - stored names are identical;
  - `defaults` and aliases are unchanged;
  - the registry is mode `600`, has no values, and `validate` passes.
- Re-apply wrote nothing (idempotent); `record CF_STAGING_TOKEN` cleared its draft flag.
- `tests/test-secret-helper.sh` 26/26; ShellCheck clean; `py_compile` passes; markdownlint clean; pre-commit and pre-push hooks passed.
